Company & Role Overview

About Hilo by Aktiia

High blood pressure is the world's most common disease, causing 18M deaths each year. At Hilo by Aktiia, we're building a world where no lives are lost to its effects — with technology that helps people take control of their health.

We're a venture-backed scale-up with $96M raised from investors in Europe and the US. Rooted in 18 years of research at the Swiss Center for Electronics and Microtechnology (CSEM), our device is the world's only medically accurate, cuffless, continuous blood pressure monitor for daily use — clinically validated and CE Marked as a Class IIa medical device, now available in 12 countries. In July, we launched in the US.

We're a remote-first company headquartered in Neuchâtel, Switzerland, united by our passion for impact and innovation.

Role overview

As Post-Market Surveillance Manager, you'll build and run our global post-market surveillance system — from complaint handling and adverse-event reporting to data trending and governance — and lead its rollout across Customer Support, QA, Regulatory, Engineering, Clinical, and Product. This is a hands-on role: you'll turn post-market insights into action that improves product quality, patient safety, and the customer experience, drawing on strong judgment, disciplined execution, and the ability to influence stakeholders globally.

Requirements

Core responsibilities

  • Design, build, and run our global post-market surveillance system — complaint handling, adverse-event/vigilance reporting, escalation, and governance — staying hands-on for complex or high-risk cases
  • Own the complaint-to-report pipeline: reportability assessments and timely, accurate adverse-event/vigilance submissions across markets (US, EU, and others)
  • Build the KPIs, dashboards, and trending methods that surface safety, quality, and customer-experience signals — and turn findings into action via CAPA, risk management, product/software fixes, and labeling updates
  • Lead the cross-functional rollout — implementation plans, priorities, dependencies, and risk — to build sustainable post-market processes and infrastructure
  • Present post-market performance and recommendations to leadership, and support PMS reports, PSURs, and management reviews
  • Act as SME during audits and inspections, and guide internal teams and external partners on post-market activities

Background & Experience

  • 7+ years in medical-device post-market surveillance, complaint handling, quality, or regulatory affairs, including leading process implementations
  • At least a bachelor's degree
  • Hands-on experience with complaint investigations, reportability assessments, and regulatory submissions (FDA MDR, EU MDR vigilance/PMS, ISO 13485, ISO 14971), plus post-market data analysis
  • Program management skills — workstreams, stakeholders, dependencies — plus an analytical mindset for turning complaint data into risk-based recommendations
  • Strong communicator, comfortable influencing cross-functional teams, leadership, and regulators
  • Hands-on, independent leadership style; able to scale processes as we grow
  • Nice to have: experience with additional international markets or digital complaint-management systems

What success looks like

  • Scalable processes for complaint intake, investigation, and resolution — with clear escalation pathways to ensure adverse events and reportable incidents are identified, assessed, and reported within regulatory timeline
  • Customer Support consistently identifies, documents, and escalates complaints and potential safety events, thanks to close partnership and training
  • KPIs and dashboards give clear visibility into complaint timeliness, resolution, regulatory reporting, and emerging trends
  • Post-market insights translate into action — product improvements, CAPAs, risk-management updates, and a better customer experience

Benefits

What Makes You A Great Fit

At Hilo by Aktiia, our values guide everything we do:

Move the Needle — You focus on what drives real impact. You let data and clarity guide your decisions, and you take accountability for results. You're a difference maker — you drive ideas to commercial success from start to end

Move Fast, Learn, Refine — You work with urgency and purpose, balancing speed with quality. You treat feedback as a chance to learn, and you're deep in customer and partner feedback — translating it to action quickly

Team First — You collaborate effectively across teams and build trust through clarity and respect. You're comfortable bridging local execution with a global team, and you communicate openly across time zones

Why Join Us?

  • Hilo by Aktiia is becoming one of the most important med-tech companies, and you can be part of this exciting story
  • Work on a mission that matters: transforming cardiovascular health at global scale
  • Be part of a high-impact, fast-growing, and venture-backed scale-up company
  • Collaborate with a diverse, passionate, and talented team
  • Competitive compensation and equity program, and other benefits (depending on location)

Ready to Move the Needle?

If you are passionate about making a meaningful impact in people's lives and excel in an environment where individuals take ownership and are committed to delivering results, we are happy to receive your application.

Job Description Summary

As the Portfolio Strategy Director, you lead portfolio strategy, executive decision support, and stakeholder alignment for complex corporate real estate initiatives. You will translate business demand, real estate supply options, stakeholder needs, financial considerations, and portfolio data into executive-ready options, tradeoffs, and portfolio actions that help clients make confident, aligned, and timely decisions.

As a member of Cushman & Wakefield’s Portfolio Advisory Group, the Portfolio Strategy Director will be dedicated to one or more of Cushman & Wakefield’s most dynamic client accounts. In this role, you will collaborate closely with peers and the account team to support a client's strategic real estate vision. The Portfolio Strategy Director will embody our team philosophy “Client First, Insight Always, Execution Excellence”, ensuring every deliverable reflects the team’s commitment to innovation, collaboration, and measurable impact.

Job Description

Portfolio Strategy & Decision Support

  • Lead portfolio strategy activities that connect business growth forecasts, utilization insights, real estate alternatives, financial considerations, and operational requirements into actionable recommendations.

  • Develop real estate scenarios that clarify options, tradeoffs, risks, dependencies, sequencing, and recommended paths forward for client and account leadership.

  • Translate business strategy and stakeholder needs into real estate requirements and initiatives, including what space is needed, where options exist, and how decisions support broader portfolio objectives.

Executive Business Case Development

  • Lead development of executive-ready business case memos for renewals, consolidations, new sites, dispositions, relocations, and capital projects.

  • Structure business cases using consistent frameworks, templates, and decision-support standards that improve clarity, comparability, and speed to decision.

  • Partner with Finance and other stakeholders to interpret financial impacts, pressure-test assumptions, and translate investment tradeoffs into executive-ready recommendations.

  • Package complex inputs into concise narratives, recommendations, FAQs, and leadership updates that support executive decision-making.

We are currently seeking a Associate Director, Vendor Management - Remote to join our team in Burnaby, British Columbia (CA-BC), Canada (CA).

Associate Director, Vendor Management

Position Summary

The Senior Hardware Procurement & Vendor Management Lead is responsible for overseeing end-to-end procurement, sourcing, vendor management, and hardware lifecycle activities for enterprise clients. The role will manage procurement operations across PC and end-user computing hardware, working closely with OEMs, distributors, resellers, Procurement, Commercial, Finance, Service Management, and client stakeholders.

This position combines strategic procurement, supplier management, hardware lifecycle planning, financial oversight, and client engagement. The successful candidate will ensure hardware requirements are met efficiently and cost-effectively while balancing client demand, inventory levels, supply chain considerations, service quality, and long-term technology roadmaps.

The role requires a strong understanding of B2B indirect procurement, hardware sourcing, vendor negotiations, managed services environments, and enterprise client management.

Key Responsibilities

Procurement & Strategic Sourcing

  • Manage and oversee day-to-day procurement activities, including requisitions, purchase orders, order fulfillment, and vendor coordination with OEMs and suppliers.
  • Lead the sourcing and quoting process for PC and end-user computing equipment, ensuring clients receive the best combination of price, quality, availability, and value.
  • Partner with Procurement leadership to manage the end-to-end procurement process and ensure compliance with established policies, controls, and commercial agreements.
  • Review supplier pricing, catalogue pricing, invoices, and payment requirements to ensure accuracy and alignment with contracted services and agreed pricing.
  • Identify opportunities for cost optimization, process improvement, and procurement efficiency.
  • Support the development and evaluation of RFPs, RFQs, supplier agreements, and procurement strategies.

Hardware Lifecycle & Roadmap Management

  • Establish and manage hardware roadmaps for Health Authorities (HAs) and provincial environments, including timelines for device transitions, refreshes, last buys, and retirement.
  • Coordinate the transition to new hardware platforms and retirement of legacy devices while minimizing operational disruption.
  • Ensure new hardware standards and associated knowledge base articles (KBAs) are established and maintained to support efficient service delivery.
  • Gather key hardware decision points and recommendations from HA stakeholders and communicate financial impacts, risks, and trade-offs.
  • Evaluate options such as hardware specifications, pricing models, purchase versus leasing, warranty coverage, and lifecycle strategies.
  • Develop and maintain provincial hardware standards and ensure alignment between HA requirements, OEM capabilities, Commercial teams, and suppliers.
  • Identify opportunities to standardize hardware and reduce complexity, cost, and support requirements.

Budget & Financial Management

  • Manage hardware budgets established by HA clients and monitor spending against approved forecasts and financial targets.
  • Identify, investigate, and address budget variances and unexpected procurement costs.
  • Analyze financial impacts associated with hardware decisions and provide recommendations to stakeholders.
  • Balance inventory investment, supply chain requirements, and client demand to minimize the cost of capital while maintaining appropriate availability.
  • Identify opportunities to reduce total cost of ownership through improved sourcing, lifecycle planning, warranty strategies, and supplier management.

Vendor & OEM Management

  • Manage strategic relationships with major PC manufacturers, OEMs, distributors, and third-party suppliers.
  • Lead regular meetings with OEMs and third-party vendors to review demand, supply, pricing, service performance, issues, and upcoming requirements.
  • Establish clear expectations for vendor performance and proactively address service, supply, pricing, and quality issues.
  • Develop and maintain supplier performance metrics and balanced scorecards in partnership with Commercial.
  • Escalate vendor issues where appropriate and drive corrective actions through to resolution.
  • Leverage supplier relationships and market knowledge to identify opportunities for improved pricing, service levels, supply continuity, and operational efficiency.

Client & Stakeholder Management

  • Lead weekly meetings with HA clients and cross-functional teams to review hardware demand, forecasts, procurement requirements, and upcoming lifecycle activities.
  • Work closely with client stakeholders to understand changing business requirements and translate them into actionable procurement and hardware strategies.
  • Present recommendations, financial impacts, risks, and trade-offs to senior stakeholders.
  • Build strong relationships with client teams and effectively manage challenging situations, competing priorities, and conflict resolution.
  • Act as a key point of contact between clients, Procurement, Commercial, OEMs, vendors, and operational teams.

Operational Improvement & Service Optimization

  • Meet regularly with frontline service and support teams to identify recurring hardware issues, operational challenges, and opportunities for improvement.
  • Analyze ServiceNow incident and service data to identify trends and problem hardware and develop proactive strategies to reduce end-user and HA impact.
  • Evaluate warranty programs, parts availability, parts lockers, break/fix models, and other support strategies to improve service quality and optimize costs.
  • Identify opportunities to improve sourcing processes, procurement tools, reporting, operational efficiency, and cost savings.
  • Develop proactive strategies for managing hardware supply, product discontinuations, quality issues, and other potential impacts to end users.
  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives across the hardware procurement and lifecycle management process.

Reporting & Governance

  • Develop and maintain balanced scorecards, procurement dashboards, forecasts, and management reporting in partnership with Commercial.
  • Provide regular reporting on hardware demand, procurement activity, supplier performance, budgets, inventory, lifecycle milestones, and risks.
  • Ensure accurate and timely reporting to support client and internal decision-making.
  • Maintain appropriate procurement documentation, records, and governance controls.

Required Qualifications & Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree required.
  • 8–12 years of progressive procurement, sourcing, vendor management, or supply chain experience, preferably within B2B indirect procurement.
  • Strong experience managing procurement operations, suppliers, and vendors within an enterprise or managed services environment.
  • Experience with SAP Ariba and ServiceNow.
  • Experience managing hardware procurement and lifecycle activities, preferably within an enterprise IT or end-user computing environment.
  • Experience working directly with enterprise clients and senior stakeholders.
  • Demonstrated experience managing challenging client situations, negotiations, escalations, and conflict resolution.
  • Experience leading and coordinating matrixed or geographically distributed teams, including overseas resources.
  • Strong experience with PC hardware manufacturers and suppliers such as Dell, HP, Lenovo, and global resellers/distributors is preferred.
  • Direct, client-facing experience is strongly preferred.

Key Skills & Competencies

  • Strong strategic sourcing and procurement expertise.
  • Excellent vendor and supplier relationship management skills.
  • Strong commercial and financial acumen.
  • Excellent analytical and problem-solving abilities.
  • Strong negotiation and influencing skills.
  • Ability to analyze complex data and translate findings into actionable recommendations.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Strong client relationship and stakeholder management capabilities.
  • Ability to manage competing priorities and operate effectively in a complex, matrixed organization.
  • Strong leadership skills with the ability to influence teams without direct authority.
  • Proactive approach to identifying risks, opportunities, and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Ability to balance cost, quality, service, availability, and client requirements when making procurement decisions.

Pay Transparency

This range reflects the minimum and maximum target compensation for the position across all US locations. Actual compensation will depend on a number of factors, including the candidate’s actual work location, relevant experience, technical skills, and other qualifications.

  • Collaborate with marketing and leadership to provide feedback on lead quality, common objections, competitor activity, and prospective family needs

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree or higher
  • Sales Experience: 3+ years of consultative sales experience, including demonstrated success closing high-ticket products or services

The ideal candidate will also possess:

  • The ability to work both independently and in a team environment
  • Excellent presentation skills
  • Ability to explain educational services offered in a clear and impactful way
  • Strong organizational and time-management abilities to be able to meet enrollment goals
  • Experience with meeting revenue goals set by organizations

Why you want to be an Admissions Sales Consultant with Vanguard College Prep:

  • Uncapped Earning Potential: Competitive compensation structure that includes commission with benefits
  • Fully Remote Flexibility: Enjoy the autonomy of working from home with regular team collaboration and support.

About Vanguard College Prep:

Vanguard College Prep is a premier, results-driven education company serving high-achieving families across the country. Our programs are built for students who want to compete at the highest levels of academic performance — from top SAT/ACT scores to elite college admissions.

Job Description

Cardiovascular Utilization Management Reviewer (Electrophysiology)

Are you ready to make a meaningful impact on patient care in a non-clinical setting? Join our Utilization Management team as a Field Medical Director, Cardiovascular Specialist and use your expertise in EP Cardiology to help ensure the delivery of high-value, evidence-based case reviews. Enjoy improved work-life balance while contributing to better health outcomes in an environment that fosters collaboration, continuous learning, and impactful peer-to-peer discussions.

  • Opportunities for collaboration with a dynamic team of physicians, leaders, and clinical professionals.

  • Current, unrestricted clinical license in medicine or required specialty

  • Obtaining and maintaining medical licenses in the state you reside, as well as, other state licensure required per business needs

    • Active Board Certification in Cardiology and proof of prior board certification in Electrophysiology

    • Active Board Certification in Cardiology and proof of active practice as an Electrophysiologist for 5+ years

  • Strong clinical, management, communication, and organizational skills

  • Energetic and curious with a passion for quality and value in health care

  • Computer Proficiency

  • No history of a major disciplinary or legal action by a state medical board

The use of artificial intelligence tools during interviews is prohibited and monitored. Misrepresentation will result in immediate disqualification from consideration.

You are a tenacious, sharp dermatology biller who knows ModMed inside and out. You treat unresolved claims as personal challenges, spot coding discrepancies before submission, and keep practice revenue flowing smoothly.

jobs.description:
Important Notice for Applicants:
At Bixal, we want to ensure a transparent and secure application process for all candidates. Official communication will come from an email address ending in @bixal.com or from @bixal.na.teamtailor-mail.com. Messages from other sources may be fraudulent, and you should exercise care to avoid any links or attachments included.

Bixal will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment.

Need Assistance or a Reasonable Accommodation?If you need assistance or a reasonable accommodation to complete your application, we're here to help. Please reach out to us at and let us know how we can support you. You do not need to share personal details or disclose the nature of your request. You can expect a response from a team member within 24 hours during the regular work week and on the next operating day during the weekend or holidays.

Why Bixal?

Bixal is a consulting company headquartered in Fairfax, VA, working alongside governments and organizations to help them deliver better services and experiences to the communities they serve. Using evidence-based knowledge and technology, Bixal empowers clients to deliver on their missions more effectively by fostering a culture of learning and continuous improvement.

Our values:

  • People-First: Emphasizing the importance of people in all aspects of work.

  • Collaboration and Transparency: Valuing teamwork and open communication.

  • Growth Mindset: Encouraging innovation and continuous improvement.

  • Creating Lasting Impact: Focusing on meaningful outcomes and positive change.

About the role:

Bixal is hiring a Senior Service Designer / UX Researcher to join our Developer Experience team on a newly awarded platform engineering contract with the Department of Education's Federal Student Aid (FSA). FSA manages nearly $1.7 trillion in federal student loans and serves more than 45 million borrowers. This contract is building the platform engineering foundation that enables FSA's engineering teams to deliver faster, more securely, and with less friction.

You will be the embedded HCD practitioner on a four-person Developer Experience team, working alongside a Technical Product Manager, a Content/Documentation Specialist, and a Software Engineer. Your job is to make the platform something developers actually want to use. You'll map the end-to-end developer journey, identify friction, run sprint-cadence usability testing, and translate research directly into the backlog. The people you're designing for are software engineers and developers, not end users of a public-facing website, and that distinction matters.

Applicants must include a link to a portfolio of relevant work.

Location:

This is a fully remote position that can be worked anywhere in the U.S. While most of the work is expected to be conducted virtually, there is potential for occasional travel for on-site meetings and working sessions (Washington, D.C.) at the discretion of the client. Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the US. Bixal does not provide visa sponsorship. U.S. citizenship is required for this position due to contractual requirement.

Compensation:

The salary range for this role is $125,000 – $130,000. In the spirit of transparency, most offers tend to land near the midpoint of the range. We make compensation decisions thoughtfully, considering your experience, the skills you bring, and our commitment to internal equity. Fairness and transparency are core to how we operate.

Responsibilities:

Research and Discovery

  • Map the end-to-end developer journey from access request through first production deploy, identifying high-friction points at each stage.

  • Plan and execute sprint-cadence user research with FSA engineering teams using methods such as contextual inquiry, usability testing, interviews, and behavioral analytics.

  • Synthesize qualitative and quantitative findings into actionable insights and translate them directly into prioritized backlog items.

  • rack adoption metrics and developer satisfaction (Developer NPS) to measure the impact of improvements over time.

Service Design

  • Design service blueprints, interaction patterns, user flows, and high-fidelity prototypes for developer-facing products including the self-service portal, onboarding toolkit, and golden-path templates.

  • Deliver design specifications and documentation that reduce implementation ambiguity and improve fidelity between design intent and what gets built.

  • Collaborate with the team’s software engineer to keep the iteration loop tight within a single sprint cadence, ensuring research-backed interaction patterns are reflected in working software.

  • Design responsive, accessible interfaces that account for regulatory and secure interaction requirements without degrading usability.

  • Apply accessibility standards (Section 508, WCAG 2.1) to all developer-facing interfaces and documentation experiences.

  • Contribute to a developer experience metrics dashboard, defining what gets measured and why.

Collaboration and Stakeholder Engagement

  • Work closely with the team’s Technical Product Manager to align research priorities with the product roadmap and QASP performance measures.

  • Engage FSA engineering stakeholders to understand their workflows, constraints, and needs, building trust and buy-in for platform adoption.

  • Participate in agile ceremonies including sprint planning, backlog refinement, demos, and retrospectives.

  • Coordinate with adjacent vendor teams and FSA stakeholders to ensure the developer experience serves the broader engineering ecosystem.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in a relevant field plus at least eight (8) years of experience in service design, UX research, or human-centered design.

  • Proven ability to design intuitive, accessible, and production-ready experiences for complex, multi-step workflows serving large user populations.

  • Demonstrated experience reducing task friction, error rates, and avoidable support contacts through measurable design improvements.

  • Strong capability designing responsive digital experiences and system-driven UI behavior in collaboration with engineering teams.

  • Experience incorporating regulatory, accessibility, and secure interaction requirements into design artifacts without degrading usability.

  • Demonstrated expertise in applied research methods including contextual inquiry, usability testing, journey mapping, service blueprinting, and synthesis of qualitative and quantitative findings.

  • Experience conducting research with technical users, developers, or platform/tool users, and the ability to adapt methods appropriately for that audience.

  • Proven ability to translate research findings directly into prioritized backlog items, high-fidelity prototypes, specifications, and design documentation that reduce ambiguity and accelerate delivery.

  • Proficiency in Figma, Miro or FigJam, or equivalent collaborative design and whiteboarding tools.

  • Familiarity with developer tools and environments (e.g., CI/CD pipelines, portals, documentation systems) sufficient to understand the context developers work in.

  • Strong communication skills with the ability to present findings clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

  • This position requires the ability to obtain and maintain a favorable Tier 4 / High Risk Public Trust determination in support of a federal government contract.

Nice to Have Skills and Experience:

  • Experience working on developer experience, internal tooling, or platform-as-product initiatives.

  • Familiarity with the U.S. Web Design System (USWDS), the 21st Century IDEA, USDS Playbook, and other federal design standards.

  • Experience working within FedRAMP, FISMA, or other federal compliance environments.

  • Familiarity with DORA metrics, DevSecOps concepts, or agile platform engineering practices.

  • Prior experience with the Department of Education or Federal Student Aid.

How We Support Our Team:

  • Flex hours

  • 401K with matching incentive

  • Parental Leave

  • Medical/dental/vision benefits

  • Flex Spending Account

  • Company provided short-term disability and life insurance

  • Commuter benefits

  • Paid Time Off (PTO)

  • 11 Paid holidays

Our company is committed to providing equal employment opportunities for all individuals and complies with all applicable federal, state, and local anti-discrimination laws. Employment decisions are based on merit, qualifications, and business needs.

Job Title: Data Acquisition Specialist - External Data (Remote - UK)

Job Location: Manchester, Greater Manchester, United Kingdom

Job Location Type: Remote

Job Contract Type: Full-time

Job Seniority Level:

The Data Acquisition Specialist performs activities relating to the definition, set-up and ingestion of External Data Streams, and related documents and processes aligned with Clinical Trial Protocol defined requirements for data capture.

External data streams include but are not limited to typical and novel data collected through central labs and ECG, medical imaging, biomarker and genomics analysis, real world data sources, EHR, electronic patient reported outcomes, wearables and sensors and other digital data collection technologies.

Deliverables

  • Execute deliverables for Standardized External Data Streams.

  • Assess external data collection requirements per protocol and planning of external data stream set-up activities and related deliverables to meet study start-up timelines.

  • Liaise with key data stakeholders to establish the purpose of data collection and requirements for the transfer, ingestion, and structure of data for each data stream in compliance with applicable data protection laws and regulations, utilizing available standards and templates

  • Create change requests for the definition of new test concepts or data structures relating to external data.

  • Develop trial-specific Data Transfer Agreements (tsDTA’s) accurately documenting study requirements and methods for the data transfer, ingestion, and structure.

  • Ensure data transfer frequencies are sufficient for the agreed requirements (medical data review, central monitoring, and reporting and analysis).

  • Liaise with external data providers to ensure alignment and agreement of tsDTA.

  • Translate medical and scientific concepts into data mapping guidance, per agreed data model and documented in the annotated Data Transfer Agreement for use by Clinical programmers.

  • UAT of test data transfers ensure accuracy and consistency with data specifications defined in Data Transfer Agreements.

  • Implement data transfer mechanisms for external data streams (into CDR) including access for external data providers.

  • Monitor availability and accuracy of external data streams, liaise with external data providers to resolve data transfer issues relating to conformance of data.

Education and Experience Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent, preferably in Computer Science.

  • Minimum of 3 years’ experience managing data in support of clinical research.

  • Experience working with external data e.g., Safety Lab, PK, Simple Biomarkers, ECG, etc

  • Experience in working with external data providers within a clinical study

    setting.

  • Experience developing data transfer agreements.

  • Experience working on clinical trials.

  • Experience working in highly diverse teams within clinical research; cross-functional, global, multiregional.

  • Knowledge of SDTM.

  • Working knowledge of GCP/ICH guidelines

  • Excellent written and verbal communication in English.

This role is not eligible for UK visa sponsorship

jobs.excerpt: About TouchBistroTouchBistro is an all-in-one restaurant management platform built to help restaurant operators run stronger, more successful businesses.
jobs.description:
About TouchBistro

TouchBistro is an all-in-one restaurant management platform built to help restaurant operators run stronger, more successful businesses. Our solutions span point of sale, payments, front-of-house and back-of-house operations, and guest engagement. As part of Harris Computer, TouchBistro combines the focus and agility of a restaurant technology company with the long-term orientation of a leading vertical market software organization.


The Opportunity

TouchBistro is seeking an experienced Vice President, Sales & Marketing to lead an integrated go-to-market organization across North America. Reporting to the EVP, this executive will translate company strategy into a focused commercial plan, build a predictable and efficient revenue engine, sharpen our market position, and develop high-performing Sales and Marketing teams.

This is a hands-on executive role for a leader who can connect market insight, product value, demand generation, sales execution, pricing, brand, content, web, analytics, and marketing operations. The successful candidate will bring clarity to how TouchBistro targets the right customers, communicates differentiated value, creates and converts demand, and measures performance from first touch through booked and live recurring revenue.

What Success Looks Like

  • A clear, company-wide commercial strategy that defines priority markets, ideal customer profiles, channel choices, value propositions, and measurable growth outcomes.
  • A predictable funnel with disciplined forecasting, strong pipeline hygiene, clear stage definitions, and transparent conversion performance from lead through booking and activation handoff.
  • Improved sales and marketing efficiency, with investment decisions grounded in customer quality, unit economics, expected lifetime value, payback, and live recurring revenue.
  • Stronger product positioning, pricing discipline, launch execution, competitive intelligence, and sales enablement across the TouchBistro portfolio.
  • One integrated Sales and Marketing operating rhythm, with shared priorities, clear accountability, fast learning cycles, and a culture of coaching and continuous improvement.

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise Growth Strategy & Leadership

  • Own the overall Sales and Marketing strategy and operating plan, aligned to TouchBistro’s business priorities, financial objectives, product roadmap, and customer strategy.
  • Translate growth objectives into market, segment, channel, capacity, investment, and talent plans with clear assumptions and measurable outcomes.
  • Lead, coach, and develop the Sales and Marketing leadership team; establish clear decision rights, performance expectations, succession plans, and career paths.
  • Create an integrated operating cadence across Sales and Marketing, including weekly execution reviews, monthly funnel and forecast reviews, and quarterly business planning.
  • Act as a key member of the executive leadership team, bringing a market- and customer-informed perspective to company strategy, resource allocation, and portfolio decisions.

Sales Strategy, Pipeline & Execution

  • Own delivery of new-business revenue targets and the commercial performance of inbound, outbound, and business development motions.
  • Build a disciplined, repeatable sales process covering lead response, qualification, discovery, demonstration, solution fit, proposal, negotiation, contracting, and close.
  • Establish consistent definitions and controls for pipeline creation, stage progression, conversion, forecast categories, sales-cycle velocity, win/loss analysis, and CRM hygiene.
  • Align account coverage, territories, quotas, capacity, and compensation with priority customer segments and expected demand.
  • Develop high-performing sales leaders and teams through structured onboarding, coaching, call review, playbooks, feedback, and clear career paths.
  • Partner with Customer Success and Operations to ensure honest expectations, clean handoffs, customer readiness, and stronger conversion from sold to live.
  • Provide executive sponsorship for strategic prospects, customers, RFPs, and complex commercial negotiations when appropriate.

Demand Generation & Revenue Marketing

  • Set the inbound and outbound demand generation strategy across paid search, SEO, lifecycle nurture, paid social, website, events, webinars, account-based programs, and other relevant channels.
  • Allocate budgets across markets, audiences, and channels based on pipeline contribution, customer quality, conversion, ACV, payback, and return on investment.
  • Build an experimentation roadmap to improve audience targeting, offer design, channel mix, lead quality, conversion, and speed to learning.
  • Create tight alignment between Marketing and Sales on campaign priorities, service-level expectations, lead routing, follow-up, qualification, and feedback loops.
  • Balance short-term pipeline creation with long-term category credibility, brand strength, customer advocacy, and organic demand.

Product Marketing, Pricing & Go-to-Market

  • Own the commercial articulation of TouchBistro’s value proposition, product positioning, messaging architecture, proof points, and differentiation by customer segment and use case.
  • Lead go-to-market planning and execution for new products, bundles, features, releases, and market entries in partnership with Product, Sales, Customer Success, Finance, and Operations.
  • Build a disciplined pricing and packaging capability informed by customer value, competitive dynamics, willingness to pay, margin, attach potential, and long-term unit economics.
  • Institutionalize market and competitive intelligence and translate insights into positioning, enablement, pricing, roadmap input, and commercial action.
  • Ensure Sales has the tools, training, battlecards, pricing guidance, customer stories, presentations, and collateral required to sell value consistently.

Brand, Content, Community & Communications

  • Define and protect TouchBistro’s brand strategy, voice, narrative, and standards across digital and traditional customer touchpoints.
  • Oversee an integrated content strategy spanning thought leadership, SEO and answer-engine visibility, product content, customer stories, newsletters, nurture, social media, events, podcasts, webinars, and sales collateral.
  • Ensure content is grounded in restaurant operator needs, product value, customer evidence, industry trends, and clear business objectives across the funnel.
  • Strengthen community engagement, customer advocacy, employee advocacy, and social listening while ensuring timely, consistent brand interaction.
  • Use research and original insights to build credibility in restaurant technology and create reusable demand, PR, sales, partner, and customer assets.

Digital Experience & Web

  • Treat the website and digital ecosystem as core commercial products that support discovery, education, conversion, and customer trust.
  • Own the web roadmap, conversion strategy, user journeys, landing-page effectiveness, accessibility, SEO foundations, performance, scalability, and content-management governance.
  • Use analytics, behavioral data, experimentation, and A/B testing to continuously improve digital conversion and campaign performance.
  • Ensure web development, design, content, product marketing, demand generation, and marketing operations work from shared priorities and measurable outcomes.
  • Oversee external agencies and vendors where needed, with clear scope, accountability, quality standards, and return expectations.

Marketing Operations, Data & Technology

  • Own marketing processes, automation, campaign operations, lead management, attribution, data quality, consent and governance, and the effectiveness of the marketing technology stack.
  • Ensure reliable integration between marketing platforms and CRM, with clear lifecycle definitions, routing, scoring, source tracking, and closed-loop reporting.
  • Develop dashboards that connect activity and spend to pipeline, booked ACV, live ACV, customer quality, payback, and retention-relevant indicators.
  • Create a trusted performance narrative by combining data with actionable insight, identifying root causes, and recommending clear management actions.
  • Simplify tools and workflows, automate repetitive work, and use AI responsibly to improve targeting, content operations, seller productivity, analysis, and speed of execution.

Cross-Functional Commercial Alignment

  • Partner closely with Product to bring customer and competitive insight into roadmap choices, business cases, packaging, launches, and lifecycle decisions.
  • Partner with Finance on targets, budgets, forecast assumptions, unit economics, deal quality, pricing governance, and investment trade-offs.
  • Partner with Customer Success and Operations to improve sales-to-activation handoffs, surface expectation gaps, support retention, and create customer expansion and advocacy opportunities.
  • Build strong relationships with strategic customers and ecosystem partners and represent TouchBistro at relevant industry events and executive forums.
  • Promote direct communication, clear ownership, and shared metrics across the full customer journey.

Performance Management

The VP will establish a concise executive scorecard and use it to drive decisions, accountability, and continuous improvement. Measures are expected to include:


Growth : Booked ACV, live ACV, new recurring revenue, average deal size, attainment by channel and segment

Funnel : Pipeline coverage, lead-to-opportunity conversion, win rate, sales-cycle velocity, forecast accuracy

Efficiency : Sales and Marketing spend to live ACV, CAC and payback, channel ROI, quota capacity and productivity

Customer quality : Ideal-customer mix, sold-to-kickoff and sold-to-live conversion, early-life churn indicators, expectation quality

Marketing : Qualified pipeline contribution, website conversion, content and nurture influence, attribution quality, brand and share-of-voice indicators

Execution : CRM hygiene, speed to lead, campaign delivery, launch readiness, pricing compliance, enablement adoption

People : Engagement, retention, leadership bench strength, ramp time, coaching effectiveness, succession coverage

Qualifications & Experience

  • 10+ years of progressive commercial leadership experience across Sales, Marketing, business development, revenue growth, or related functions, including significant leadership-of-leaders responsibility.
  • Proven success leading an integrated go-to-market organization in B2B SaaS, vertical market software, payments, restaurant technology, hospitality technology, or a comparable high-volume commercial environment.
  • Demonstrated accountability for revenue targets, demand generation, pipeline management, forecasting, pricing, budgets, and commercial performance.
  • Strong command of SaaS unit economics, funnel analytics, attribution, customer acquisition, payback, retention dynamics, and investment trade-offs.
  • Experience building disciplined sales processes and coaching teams across inbound, outbound, transactional, and complex sales motions.
  • Experience leading product marketing, positioning, messaging, go-to-market launches, pricing and packaging, competitive intelligence, and sales enablement.
  • Working knowledge of modern marketing operations, CRM, automation, analytics, web conversion, content, SEO, lifecycle marketing, and AI-enabled workflows.
  • Strong executive presence, commercial judgment, negotiation skills, and the ability to communicate clearly with employees, customers, partners, and senior stakeholders.
  • A builder’s mindset: strategic enough to set direction, analytical enough to challenge assumptions, and hands-on enough to improve execution.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Marketing, Commerce, or a related field; equivalent experience will be considered. MBA is an asset.
  • Restaurant, hospitality, POS, payments, or multi-location software experience is a strong asset.
  • English required; French is a strong asset for the Canadian market. Ability to travel within North America as required.

Leadership Profile

Commercially rigorous : Makes allocation and pricing decisions using evidence, unit economics, and customer value.

Customer-centered : Understands restaurant operators and insists that promises, products, and delivery stay aligned.

Clear and accountable : Sets a small number of priorities, assigns ownership, and addresses gaps directly and constructively.

Integrated thinker : Connects brand, product, demand, sales, activation, retention, and expansion rather than optimizing silos.

Talent builder : Develops leaders, raises the performance bar, and creates a coaching culture with visible career paths.

Adaptive operator : Tests, learns, and changes course quickly without sacrificing standards, data quality, or customer trust.

What We Offer

  • A high-impact executive mandate with direct influence on TouchBistro’s growth strategy and operating model.
  • The opportunity to lead an established Sales and Marketing organization through its next stage of focus, integration, and performance.
  • A collaborative environment with access to the broader Harris Computer network and long-term operating perspective.
  • Flexible work arrangements, competitive executive compensation with performance-based incentives, and comprehensive benefits.
  • Salary range: $120,000–$150,000 CAD annually, depending on experience.

Application & Equal Opportunity

*Only selected candidates will be contacted.

Harris is committed to an equal employment opportunity program, and applications from members of designated groups, including women, persons with disabilities, Indigenous peoples, and visible minorities, are encouraged. If you are a person with a disability, you may request assistance with the recruitment and selection process.

Harris’s Talent Acquisition team does not use text messages to communicate with candidates or to solicit confidential information. Candidates will be contacted either by a Harris manager or a member of the Talent Acquisition team for an interview, provided they meet the required qualifications.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Global Risk and Compliance
jobs.excerpt: We are looking for a Director, Global Risk & Compliance to establish and lead the firm's first centralized risk management and compliance function.
jobs.description:
We are looking for a Director, Global Risk & Compliance to establish and lead the firm's first centralized risk management and compliance function. This role will build the enterprise risk framework, develop and implement global policies (AI governance, data privacy, vendor risk management, ESG compliance), manage the corporate insurance program, and coordinate compliance execution across all regions.

This role will serve as the client-facing risk leader, engaging directly with enterprise clients on compliance questionnaires, security assessments, and risk governance. The role partners closely with the VP of IT and Sr. Security Engineer to ensure the enterprise risk framework reflects both business and technology dimensions.

This is a governance and framework role, not a technical security engineering role. The Director defines risk policy and requirements ("what" and "why"); the Sr. Security Engineer implements at the infrastructure level ("how"). The two roles operate as complements with a clear boundary.

Core Responsibilities

Risk Management & Oversight

  • Partner with executive leadership to define Blend360's risk appetite and tolerance thresholds; translate those into a practical risk management framework with clear escalation protocols across all the global enterprise.
  • Create and maintain a master risk register that tracks business, operational, regulatory, and technology risks; record who owns each risk, its likelihood and potential impact, and how we'll address it
  • Run annual risk reviews across all regions and business units; use the external Global Risk Assessment (expected Q3 2026) to benchmark our findings
  • Design incident response procedures and lead after-incident reviews to track fixes to completion
  • Brief senior leadership quarterly on our risk position, new threats, and progress on mitigation efforts

AI Governance & Technology Risk

  • Create and maintain policies for how Blend360 uses AI, manages data, handles information security, and maintains business continuity
  • Partner with the AI Steering Committee to ensure AI is used responsibly both for client work and internal operations
  • Set standards for building and using AI models: establish rules around data quality, model performance, bias detection, and responsible use; translate regulatory requirements (EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF) into Blend360 standards
  • Work with the VP of IT and Sr. Security Engineer to assess risks in our technology infrastructure (AWS, Snowflake, client systems); document findings in the risk register and present to leadership
  • Track data safety across the company, from how it's collected and processed to how it's shared and moved across borders (for both client and internal data)
  • Review client projects for risks related to cloud, data, and AI components; provide risk-based recommendations to support legal review and deal decisions

Vendor & Third-Party Risk Management

  • Establish standards for evaluating vendor and partner risks; assess key technology providers (AWS, Snowflake), subcontractors, regional partners and any data processors
  • Set rules for how we safely integrate with and share data with vendors
  • Review the technical side of partnerships, acquisitions, and client solutions working with the VP of IT
  • Review all policies at least annually and maintain an update process when policies change

Insurance & Compliance Program

  • Manage Blend360's global insurance programs: professional liability, cyber, directors & officers, general liability, and any client-specific coverage
  • Manage broker relationships and lead annual insurance renewals
  • Lead SOC 2 compliance: own the audit relationship, framework, and track remediation; work with the Sr. Security Engineer on technical requirements
  • Oversee ESG compliance, including Mastercard requirements and sustainability reporting (SBTi, CDP)
  • Track regulatory changes across North America, Europe, and Latin America that affect Blend360 (GDPR, EU AI Act, data privacy laws, employment law)

Cross-Regional Coordination

  • Coordinate compliance across regions with legal leads: North America, Latin America, and EMEA
  • Work with VP Ops in Uruguay and India on compliance, employment law, and data protection at each office
  • Fill the EMEA compliance gap until dedicated legal resources are in place; own EMEA policies in the meantime
  • Partner with legal lead on Latin American regulatory issues; work with Legal & Compliance Analyst for on-the-ground support
  • Run quarterly compliance reviews with each region; track fixes and report status to the SVP Finance

Client-Facing Risk & Compliance

  • Represent Blend360 on risk and compliance matters with enterprise clients; engage directly with their security, procurement, and compliance teams
  • Handle client compliance questionnaires (security, privacy, ESG, AI governance) in partnership with IT, Security, and delivery teams
  • Create standard checklists for reviewing client contracts and define when to escalate
  • Support high-risk contract reviews; assess insurance, liability, indemnification, and IP issues
  • Maintain a log of client contracts that exceed our risk limits

Operating Model: Risk Director vs. Sr. Security Engineer

This role works closely with the Sr. Security Engineer (reports to VP IT). The split is:

Risk Director owns: risk framework, policies, risk register, insurance, ESG, SOC 2 audits, client compliance, AI governance policy, vendor standards, cross-regional coordination, executive reporting

Sr. Security Engineer owns: AWS security, Snowflake security, access controls, vulnerability management, technical incident response, infrastructure hardening

Shared: SOC 2 (Risk owns the framework and audit; Engineer provides technical details), client questionnaires (Risk owns responses; Engineer provides technical input), AI risk (Risk owns policy; Engineer implements technical controls)

Required Qualifications

  • 8+ years in risk management, compliance, or legal operations in professional services, technology, AI/data, or consulting
  • 5+ years in a global or multi-regional role managing policies and compliance programs
  • Deep knowledge of data privacy laws (GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, LGPD), AI governance (EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF), and risk management standards (COSO, ISO 31000)
  • Technology literacy: understand cloud architecture (AWS), data platforms (Snowflake, Databricks), and AI/ML risks (bias, data quality, model drift). Not expected to build systems, but must speak credibly with technical teams and translate tech risk into business terms
  • Experience managing corporate insurance (professional liability, cyber, D&O) and working with brokers
  • Comfortable engaging directly with Fortune 500 clients on security, compliance, and risk matters
  • Strong written and verbal communication; able to present to executives, boards, and clients
  • Proven ability to influence across regions and functions in a fast-moving, matrixed organization
  • Bachelor's degree required; JD, MBA, or relevant advanced degree preferred

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in AI/ML services, data analytics, cloud-native, or digital transformation firms
  • Certifications: CRISC, CISM, CISA, CIPP/E, ARM, or equivalent
  • SOC 2 audit experience and ESG/sustainability reporting (CDP, SBTi)
  • Knowledge of cybersecurity frameworks (NIST CSF, ISO 27001) at a governance level
  • Spanish language skills
  • Familiarity with Latin American regulations (Colombia, Uruguay)
  • Experience building a compliance function from scratch at a growth-stage company

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

Blend is a premier AI services provider, committed to co-creating meaningful impact for its clients through the power of data science, AI, technology, and people. With a mission to fuel bold visions, Blend tackles significant challenges by seamlessly aligning human expertise with artificial intelligence. The company is dedicated to unlocking value and fostering innovation for its clients by harnessing world-class people and data-driven strategy. We believe that the power of people and AI can have a meaningful impact on your world, creating more fulfilling work and projects for our people and clients. For more information, visit .

  • Competitive Spanish HR & Benefits market with noisy prospects

  • Selling a complex value proposition (not a simple “nice to have”)

  • Maintaining consistency, discipline, and energy over time

👤 You

  • First experience in sales, business development, or outbound roles

You’ll probably find this frustrating if…

LinkedIn Profile:

Profile Snapshot:

Apply with your LinkedIn or upload your CVin English.

Interview Process

  • Initial Recruiter Screening

What Happens After You Apply

Right after you apply, you’ll receive an email invitation from Spark Hire to record your Intro Video. This short, self-recorded video is the final step that completes your application.

Instead of repeating yourself through multiple screening calls, you’ll introduce yourself once, and your video will be shared with the hiring team. This helps hiring managers evaluate your communication style early, making future interviews more meaningful while reducing unnecessary interview rounds.

Don’t overthink it—you can record your video as many times as you’d like before submitting it. Only your final submission will be reviewed. Please keep an eye on both your inbox and spam folder for your Spark Hire invitation.

jobs.description:
A NOTE ON HOW TO REACH US

We're truly grateful that so many people have Foundant on their radar — it means a lot that our work resonates with others. That said, due to the high volume of direct messages and emails we receive, cold outreach isn't the preferred way to be considered for a role, and we're not able to prioritize applications submitted this way. To apply for open positions, please visit our careers page, which is the fastest and most effective route to being considered.

About Foundant

At Foundant, we build mission-critical software for the social good ecosystem — helping foundations, grantmakers, nonprofits, and community organizations streamline their work, strengthen relationships, and maximize their impact. We serve the giving community worldwide with a comprehensive suite of solutions spanning grant management, community foundation software, and giving analytics.

We're a unified company shaped by strong roots across our product portfolio, and we operate with intention and purpose. Our team of ~350 people across six countries is connected by a shared North Star: to be the trusted partner and strategic advisor to the communities we serve.

Role overview

Foundant is growing its presence in the Australian philanthropic and social good sector, and we're looking for a hands-on marketing generalist to build our audience, presence, and lead pipeline on the ground. This person will grow and diversify our Australian contact list, build marketing partnerships that extend our reach across the country, run in-market events, and produce or manage the content that drives demand generation — with a distinct focus on Australian philanthropy. A talented, driven and self-directed marketing generalist who has spent 7+ years working independently in marketing across tech (and preferably philanthropy or the social good sector) who is comfortable owning a full SaaS remit — from list building to live events to content and email output — without a large team on the same timezone.

Where You’ll Work:

  • As a remote-first workplace, we believe in offering flexibility and the freedom to work where it suits you best, while staying connected through technology. Our global network of talent is supported by physical office hubs and virtual collaboration, fostering a dynamic environment where innovation and growth thrive.
  • Must be located in the same time zone as a major Australian city (e.g. Sydney, Melbourne, or Brisbane — AEST/AEDT) to overlap with events, partners, and the broader team. This role will work closely day-to-day with the small Australia-based sales team and Managing Director on local priorities, and closely within the broader marketing team — mostly based in the US — for demand-gen support, campaign alignment, content planning, and reporting.
WhatYou’llDo:

List building & marketing partnerships

  • Grow Foundant's Australian marketable list through multipronged organic, paid, and partnership-driven channels. Drive and hit monthly MQL targets.
  • Identify, pitch, and manage co-marketing and channel partnerships with sector associations, philanthropy networks, associations and philantrophy “influencers” as well as complementary vendors to extend Foundant’s reach and awareness across the country.

Events on the ground

  • Plan and run in-person events across Australia — from small roundtables, lunch and learns, webinars, to larger panels and conference presences — end to end (venue, logistics, speakers, promotion, follow-up).
  • Represent Foundant as needed at relevant industry conferences and sector gatherings.

Content & demand generation

  • Develop demand-generation content specific to the Australian philanthropic sector: webinars, panels, reports, and blog posts.
  • Either write this content directly or manage freelance/contract writers to produce it, depending on volume and specialization needed.
  • Repurpose and localize existing Foundant content (US/UK) for the Australian market and voice where appropriate.
  • Coordinate with the US-based marketing team on campaign timing, assets, and performance reporting.
  • Identify Australian clients for case studies.

Digital and Website

  • Build up Foundant's Australian LinkedIn following through targeted, locally relevant content.
  • Maintain light, timely coverage of the Foundant website for the Australian market during Australian business hours.
  • Work with the digital marketing manager on keyword strategy for paid search and Google Ads targeting the Australian market.
  • Support lead generation and conversion through SEO and AEO (answer engine optimization) for Australian search and AI-assistant visibility.
WhatYou’llNeed:
  • 7+ years of marketing experience, across different disciplines, with a significant portion working independently, building a sector, launching into a market and building a list (not just as part of a large in-house team).
  • Background in marketing for tech/SaaS.
  • A demand-gen-first mindset: you default to thinking in terms of pipeline and list growth, and treat every piece of content, event, or partnership as a lead-generation opportunity.
  • Strong writing and editorial skills — able to write compelling publication-ready emails, content and to brief, edit, and manage other writers.
  • Strong product marketing skills. Able to take the positioning of the products and translate them, and new releases, to specific markets and sectors.
  • Experience building and executing in-person events, ideally in Australia or a similar market.
  • Comfort working autonomously across a broad remit, prioritizing across list growth, partnerships, events, and content.
  • Familiarity with demand-generation fundamentals (campaigns, lead capture, webinars) and reporting on results.

Nice to have

  • Existing relationships within the Australian philanthropic or grantmaking ecosystem or a keen interest.
  • Experience in marketing in the philanthropic/nonprofit sector.
  • Experience with grant management or fundraising software, or adjacent nonprofit tech
  • Prior experience standing up a market presence from scratch (rather than scaling an existing one).
Why You’ll Love Working at Foundant:
  • At the heart of everything we do is a commitment to innovation and making a positive impact. Whether you’re working on projects that empower not-for-profits, community foundations, or corporations, your contributions will help drive real-world change.
  • We offer competitive salary and benefits, including tuition, and lifestyle reimbursements, and bespoke mindfulness and fitness initiatives.
  • With our Flexible PTO policy, you’ll have the freedom to manage your time in a way that supports your personal well-being and professional success.
  • We’re committed to your professional and personal development. With our merger, you'll have the chance to collaborate across teams, giving you exposure to diverse ideas, expertise, and projects that span multiple industries.
  • As part of a larger organization, you’ll have even more opportunities to grow your career. Whether it’s exploring new roles, leadership opportunities, or shifting to a different department, we support internal mobility to help you achieve your career goals
  • You’ll enjoy autonomy and responsibility, empowering you to approach your work creatively and independently, fostering innovation and independent thought.
  • Employee recognition is a core part of our culture. When you do a great job, we make sure everyone knows about it!

Foundant is an equal opportunity employer, committed to building a diverse workforce that represents the communities we serve. The role covers both halves of that work: the core health plan systems and platforms Belong has already built and operates for its partners, and the new set of AI capabilities, including agentic systems, that will extend those platforms and change how the work gets done.

The Chief Product Officer sets product strategy, owns the roadmap, and works alongside engineering, clinical, operations, and compliance leaders to ship software that runs real Medicare Advantage business. Belong Health partners with regional health plans to launch and scale Medicare Advantage Special Needs Plans, including Dual Eligible (D-SNP) and Chronic Condition (C-SNP) plans, and is venture backed and fully distributed across the United States. With roughly 85 people in the company, this is a hands-on job: the person in it will write specifications, sit in partner meetings, and build a small senior team rather than manage a large organization.

Essential job duties and responsibilities

  • Own the product vision for the Belong platform and turn it into a roadmap with clear sequencing, staffing, and delivery dates.
  • Decide where AI changes how the platform works and where it does not, and defend those decisions with evidence rather than enthusiasm.
  • Make build, buy, and partner calls, including decisions about core administrative processing systems and other vendor platforms.
  • Bring a point of view on how Belong packages and prices its platform for health plan partners.
  • Lead the design and delivery of AI capabilities, including agentic systems, across care management, member and provider engagement, utilization management, claims and encounter workflows, and back office operations.
  • Set the standards for model selection, evaluation, monitoring, and human oversight. Every AI capability needs a measurable quality bar before it touches regulated or member-facing work.
  • Work with security and compliance on data governance for protected health information used in AI systems, including vendor review, business associate agreements, and audit trails.
  • Track the outside market closely enough to know what Belong should build, what it should buy, and what it should wait on.
  • Own the existing health plan systems: enrollment, care management, member and provider engagement, quality and Star Ratings reporting, risk adjustment support, and partner analytics.
  • Keep the platform current with CMS requirements and with Model of Care obligations, working with compliance and clinical leadership.
  • Lower the cost to serve each member while holding or improving service levels and audit performance.
  • Run planning, prioritization, and release management across product and engineering.
  • Set and report product metrics, including adoption, cycle time, defect rates, cost to serve, and partner satisfaction.
  • Manage vendor and platform relationships, including contract scope, service levels, and escalation.
  • Serve as the product voice in prospective partner diligence, finalist presentations, and contracting.
  • Translate partner requirements into roadmap decisions without letting the platform fragment into one-off builds.
  • Support board reporting and fundraising with a clear account of what the technology does, what it costs, and what it returns.

Supervisory responsibilities

  • Direct reports include product management, design, and technical leads.
  • Hire, coach, and retain product managers, designers, and technical leads. Build a small senior team that produces a large amount of work.
  • Partner with clinical, operations, actuarial, finance, and compliance leaders on shared goals and shared accountability.
  • Contribute to company strategy as a member of the senior leadership team.

Required professional experience and qualifications

  • Twelve or more years in product management or product engineering leadership, including five or more years leading a product function at the vice president level or above.
  • Direct experience building software for health plans or risk-bearing provider organizations. Medicare Advantage experience is required.
  • Ownership of an enterprise platform through at least one full build and scale cycle, from concept to production use by paying customers.
  • Hands-on experience delivering machine learning or AI features to production, including at least one agentic or large language model based system operating in a regulated environment.
  • Working knowledge of the CMS requirements that shape plan operations: enrollment, encounter and claims data, Star Ratings, risk adjustment, appeals and grievances, and Model of Care.
  • Experience with HIPAA and protected health information handling, vendor security review, and audit readiness.
  • Record of shipping with a small team and a constrained budget.

Preferred professional experience and qualifications

  • Experience at a Series B through Series D company, including work through a period of financial constraint or restructuring.
  • Special Needs Plan experience, particularly D-SNP or C-SNP product design and operations.
  • Familiarity with core administrative processing systems.
  • Experience selling to or serving regional Blue Cross Blue Shield plans or provider-sponsored health plans.
  • Comfortable with ambiguity and willing to make decisions before the data is complete.
  • Direct in communication. Raises problems early and in writing.
  • Credible with clinicians, actuaries, and engineers in the same meeting.
  • Motivated by the outcome for members who are dually eligible or living with chronic conditions.

Education, training, license and certification

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent professional experience.
  • Advanced degree in a technical, clinical, or business field preferred.

About Keyfactor

Our mission is to securely connect the world: humans, machines, and AI. Keyfactor is the leader in trust infrastructure for AI and machines, helping the world's largest enterprises and government agencies take control of the cryptographic identities that safeguard every digital interaction. Behind the platform is a global team of people who care deeply about the work and each other. We move fast, think big, and show up for one another every day. If you're looking for work that matters and a team that brings out your best, we hope you'll trust your future with Keyfactor!

Title: Director, Customer Marketing

Location: United States; Remote or Canada

Experience: Director

Job Function: Marketing

Employment Type: Full-time

Industry: Computer & Network Security

About the position

The fastest revenue Keyfactor will ever win comes from the customers we have already won. As enterprises consolidate their machine identity and cryptography investments onto fewer platforms, the companies that grow are the ones whose customers realize value, renew, expand, and advocate. Keyfactor is investing in exactly that and we are looking for a Director of Customer Marketing to lead it.
Reporting to the Vice President of Product & Customer Marketing, this role owns how Keyfactor engages and grows its customer base across four outcomes: customers realize value, stay, grow, and advocate. You will lead the customer marketing and community team, own the strategy and operating model for marketing to the installed base, and build the programs behind it into one connected system with measurable revenue impact.
This is a highly cross-functional role with strong influence across Customer Success, Sales, Product, and the broader marketing organization. Customer marketing is also one of Keyfactor's richest channels for customer insight: programs like the community and customer events surface what customers need next, and this role turns that signal into structured input for product roadmap and go-to-market strategy.

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States or Canada.

Responsibilities

• Define and lead Keyfactor's customer marketing strategy across adoption, retention, expansion, and advocacy, building a connected program calendar the business can plan against.
• Drive awareness and adoption across the installed base, helping customers discover and use the capabilities they own and the solutions they have not yet adopted, in partnership with Customer Success and Product Marketing.
• Build renewal and expansion programs in partnership with Revenue Marketing, Sales, and Customer Success, engaging accounts ahead of renewal windows and running cross-sell campaigns keyed to product whitespace and adoption signals.
• Own the customer advocacy and referral engine, including references, case studies, customer speakers, reviews, and referral programs that supply Sales, Revenue Marketing, and Analyst Relations with proof and introductions.
• Lead and develop the community manager, who owns the Keyfactor Community, setting direction and investment and connecting community engagement to retention and expansion outcomes.
• Own the strategy and evolution of the customer advisory board and executive engagement programs, guiding recruiting, agendas, and follow-through, and holding the programs to measurable member outcomes.
• Set the strategy for the customer experience at Keyfactor Connect and Keyfactor Tech Days in partnership with Field Marketing, Events and Brand, sharpening how these flagship moments drive engagement, advocacy, and pipeline.
• Channel customer insight to Product, using programs such as the community, the advisory board, and customer events to surface what customers need next and bringing structured input into roadmap and go-to-market conversations.
• Establish measurement for the function, including adoption influence, retention and expansion influence, advocacy output, and community engagement, reported in the company operating rhythm.
• Lead, develop, and grow the customer marketing and community team.

Skills and Qualification

• 8+ years in B2B enterprise marketing, with significant leadership of customer marketing, lifecycle, advocacy, or community programs.
• Proven success building retention and expansion programs in a sales-led enterprise motion, with clear measurement of revenue impact.
• Experience standing up or running customer advisory boards, executive engagement programs, or flagship customer events.
• Track record building advocacy, reference, and referral programs that supply sales, marketing, and analyst relations.
• Strong command of CRM and marketing automation data, with the ability to segment an installed base, run campaigns against it, and measure what happened.
• Experience leading and developing marketing teams, and partnering closely with Customer Success, Sales, Product, and Marketing.
• Strong written, verbal, and presentation skills, with the ability to communicate effectively across customer, field, and executive audiences.
• Experience in cybersecurity or enterprise infrastructure software is a significant advantage.

Compensation

Salary will be commensurate with experience. 

Culture, Career Opportunities and Benefits

We build teams that continually strive to get better than the day before. You will be challenged daily and given opportunities to grow personally and professionally. We balance autonomy and structure to create an entrepreneurial environment to spur creativity and new ideas. 

Here are just some of the initiatives that make our culture special:  

  • Second Fridays (a company-wide day off on the second Friday of every month minus November and December due to the Holiday schedule). Please note that this benefit is subject to change.
  • Comprehensive benefit coverage globally.
  • Paid Parental Leave is available to new parents. Structure varies based on regional/government requirements. In regions where government-paid leave doesn’t exist, like in the U.S., the company offers generous paid parental leave, along with comprehensive adoption and fertility support.
  • Competitive time off globally.
  • Dedicated employee-focused ambassadors via Key Contributors & Culture Committees.
  • DIVERSE Commitment, a call to action for a more inclusive and diverse future in business, society, and technology.
  • The Keyfactor Alliance Program to support DEIB efforts.
  • Wellbeing resources, wellness allowance, mindfulness app free membership, Wellness Wednesdays.
  • Global Volunteer Day, company non-profit matching, and 3 volunteer days off.
  • Monthly Talent development and Cross Functional meetings to support professional development.
  • Regular All Hands meetings – followed by group gatherings.

Our Core Values

Our core values are extremely important to how we run our business and what we look for in every team member:  

Trust is paramount.  

We deliver security software and solutions where trust and openness are of the highest importance for our customers. We are honest and a trusted partner in every aspect of business.  

Customers are core.  

We strategize, operate, and execute through a customer-centric view. We prioritize the security interests of our customers, and we act as if their data were our own.  

Innovation never stops, it only accelerates.
