jobs.excerpt: About VictoriaMetricsWe are the company behind the popular open-source, high-performance time-series database and monitoring solution of the same name: VictoriaMetrics.
jobs.description:
About VictoriaMetrics

We are the company behind the popular open-source, high-performance time-series database and monitoring solution of the same name: VictoriaMetrics. We’ve also recently introduced our open source logs management solution, VictoriaLogs as well as a new open source database for traces, VictoriaTraces.

Fortune 500 companies use our products as their core observability solution. Our services are used by Spotify, WIX, Grammarly, CERN and thousands others. Our open source products have been downloaded 1B+ times to date.

About the Role

We are looking for a Senior Solution Engineer who lives in the terminal and is passionate about system performance. In this role, you will be a key technical expert and the bridge between the Enterprise version of our open source Observability platform and our customers' most complex Linux-based infrastructures.

You won't just be selling software; you will be consulting with principal Software Engineers and Development Leads to help them instrument their applications, derive the best solution for their specific footprint, and gain actionable visibility into their distributed systems. As a Senior member of the team, you will focus on handling our most complex technical engagements and working closely with our Development team.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Technical Discovery & Consultation

  • Partner with Enterprise Sales to lead technical discovery for our largest strategic accounts, digging deep into the customer's current monitoring stack (metrics, logs, traces) and observability needs.

  • Consult with customers to analyze their infrastructure footprint (On-prem Linux, Cloud, Hybrid) and derive the most efficient, high-performance solution architecture using our Enterprise capabilities.

  • Act as a trusted advisor on observability and instrumentation best practices, articulating the distinct value of Enterprise features (such as advanced security, multi-tenancy, and downsampling) compared to the open source offering.

Advanced Solution Design & Demonstration

  • Architect and demonstrate sophisticated use cases for observability.

  • Lead the design and execution of complex Proof of Concepts (POCs) that prove value by instrumenting real workloads, often requiring hands-on work with Linux agents or OpenTelemetry collectors.

  • Architect scalable deployment plans for our agents/collectors across large-scale infrastructure (Kubernetes clusters, VMs, bare metal).

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Work closely with the Development team to translate customer requirements into technical specifications and provide feedback on product capabilities.

  • Collaborate with the dedicated Support team to ensure technical success during complex Proof of Concepts and seamless handoffs for new customers.

  • Collaborate with Product Management to advocate for strategic features that support the evolving landscape of cloud-native infrastructure (e.g., eBPF, WASM).

  • Create advanced technical content (white papers, blog posts, sample dashboards, scripts) that establishes authority in the engineering community.

Qualifications

Must-Haves

  • Experience: 5+ years in Pre-Sales, SRE, DevOps, or Systems Engineering roles, with a proven track record of managing complex technical sales cycles.

  • Linux Mastery: You are an expert in the terminal. You know how to troubleshoot CPU spikes, memory leaks, and disk I/O bottlenecks using standard Linux tools (top, strace, tcpdump, vmstat) and can teach others how to do the same.

  • Observability DNA: Deep understanding of the "Three Pillars" (Logs, Metrics, Traces) and the business value of reducing MTTR (Mean Time To Resolve).

  • Problem Solving: You approach troubleshooting through the lens of observability. You can diagnose why metrics are missing, identify high-cardinality churn, optimize slow queries, or determine why alerts are failing to trigger.

Technical Skills

  • OS Internals: Deep knowledge of Linux distributions (RedHat/CentOS, Ubuntu, Debian) and core concepts (Systemd, File Systems, Networking).

  • Observability Tools: Experience with metrics products such as Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, ELK Stack (Elasticsearch, Logstash, Kibana), Splunk, or Datadog.

  • Containerization: Hands-on experience with Docker and container principles.

  • Scripting: Proficiency in Bash and at least one high-level language (Python, Go, or Ruby) for automation.

  • Networking: Understanding of TCP/IP, DNS, HTTP/S, and Load Balancing.

Nice-to-Haves

  • Experience with Kubernetes (instrumenting sidecars, DaemonSets, Helm charts) at scale.

  • Knowledge of at least one SSO provider and authentication workflows.

  • Advanced proficiency with PromQL for constructing complex queries.

  • Familiarity with Infrastructure as Code (ArgoCD, Terraform, Ansible, SaltStack).

  • Experience contributing to open-source projects.

Why You'll Love Working Here

  • Competitive Base Salary.

  • Remote-first culture / Flexible PTO.

  • Passionate team members.

  • Startup atmosphere.

Our mission is to prepare promising students for meaningful lives as principled leaders. We focus on developing the whole student—academically, personally, and socially—through strong relationships, engaging content, and a vibrant online community.

We are committed to creating a learning environment that is flexible, supportive, and built around each student’s unique needs—helping them grow, think critically, and thrive both in school and beyond.

Position Summary

The Special Education Mentor supports students through a combination of co-teaching in general education settings and targeted lab instruction aligned to individualized learning needs. This role focuses on delivering specialized instruction in either Math or Language Arts/Study Skills while fostering student growth, independence, and academic success.

Reading

Writing

Math

Study Skills

      Plan and deliver instruction aligned to both general education curriculum and specialized learning needs

4) Progress Monitoring & Data Tracking

5) Collaboration & Program Support

  • Partner with academic teams to ensure alignment of support strategies

Please note that this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of the activities, duties, or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time, with or without notice.

At Mongoose, we believe every conversation matters.

We’re on a mission to change lives by making conversation intelligence accessible to all in higher education. Our purpose? To move people forward. Whether it’s helping a student navigate their first semester, connecting alumni with meaningful opportunities, or ensuring parents feel informed and supported—our AI-enabled platform drives compliant, empathetic, and impactful conversations that build trust and foster success campus-wide.

We know that conversations aren’t just a feature—they’re the foundation of connection. That’s why we focus on delivering insights, relevance, empathy, scale, and trust in everything we do. At Mongoose, we’re transforming communication in higher ed because we believe reputation is a mutual responsibility, and the right insights fuel measurable outcomes.

Join us and be part of a team that’s making a real difference in education—one conversation at a time.

As an Account Manager, you’ll be the driving force behind making sure our clients don’t just renew their contracts—they expand their use of Mongoose solutions and can’t imagine life without us. You’ll own the renewal process and lead all expansion efforts, including upsells and cross-sells, by diving deep into client relationships, uncovering their needs, and helping them achieve their goals with our products. Success in this role will be measured by increasing client retention rates, achieving both your annual renewal , and expansion quotas through adoption and growth of our Conversation Intelligence Platform. If you love building expansion pipelines through strategic account planning and referential selling and have a demonstrated history of exceeding quota, this role is for you.

What You'll Do

  • Sell and Renew with Confidence: Consistently meet or exceed assigned renewal and expansion quotas to drive revenue growth, while developing informed, strategic retention and growth plans in partnership with your Customer Success Manager. Lead renewals with confidence so clients feel valued, supported, and excited to sign on for another year (or more), and proactively anticipate and address risks well before renewal time—because surprises are for birthdays, not contracts.
  • Drive Growth Like a Pro: Build pipeline through focused weekly outbound activities, own upsell and cross-sell opportunities by showing clients how Mongoose can solve even more of their challenges, and expand our footprint within schools by introducing our solutions to new departments and teams that didn’t know they needed us—until you showed them.

Use a deep understanding of client goals and challenges to position Mongoose as an indispensable partner, and work in true partnership with a dedicated Client Success Manager—driving commercial strategy (renewals, upsells, expansions) while your CSM partner drives adoption, value realization, and day-to-day success. Together, you’re accountable for delivering outcomes that maximize satisfaction and growth.

Be the face of Mongoose for your accounts, turning relationships into partnerships and partnerships into growth, including onsite visits and travel as needed.
  • Make Data Your Superpower: Track client health metrics to guide conversations and uncover opportunities, maintain an accurate and squeaky-clean CRM (hello, HubSpot!) with all renewals, upsells, and interactions, and share insights and updates internally to ensure alignment and fuel smarter strategies.

What You'll Bring to the Table

You’ve demonstrated the ability to build healthy pipelines, convert with strong win rates, and successfully drive renewals while growing accounts through upsells and cross-sells. You know how to sell without feeling “salesy,” positioning solutions in ways that feel natural, helpful, and downright irresistible.
  • A Relationship Builder Extraordinaire: You’re a natural at connecting with people and building trust, making clients feel understood and supported. Your exceptional communication skills ensure even complex ideas are easy to understand and act on.
  • Proactive Problem-Solver: You don’t wait for problems to knock—you see them coming and have solutions ready before anyone else notices. As a strong, strategic thinker, you’re always looking for ways to improve processes and drive better outcomes.

You excel at translating data into actionable insights that empower clients to make informed business decisions, and you bring experience with CRM systems (bonus points for HubSpot expertise!).

Your positive, can-do attitude makes you a joy to work with for both colleagues and clients.

Why You'll Love It Here

jobs.description:
Job Title

Americas Regional Resilience & Protection Manager

Job Description Summary

A regional specialist and subject matter expert in physical protection and operational resilience for implementing and overseeing Cushman & Wakefield’s (C&W) resilience & protection strategy. Acting as an ambassador for “Enterprise Resilience & Protection” (ER&P) matters across the Americas business and supporting operational teams to develop, implement and maintain procedures, programs and initiatives covering physical protection and resilience in line with C&W policy.

Responsible for Protection at the Category 1 locations in region, and the strategic assessment of organizational protection vulnerabilities and developing strategic initiatives to minimize, control and mitigate potential threats. Prioritizing focus on protecting employees and key internal and external stakeholders from potential protection threats impacting their personal safety/protection.
This is a senior corporate role which will directly report to the Global Lead Enterprise Resilience & Protection. The role will require an experienced professional who has held a similar role in a related industry and who is comfortable and confident in working and presenting at a senior level.
The individual will be commercially aware and fully accountable for developing productive relationships with key service line stakeholders for the region.

Job Description

Core Responsibilities:

This Americas Regional Resilience & Protection role will be responsible for identifying areas of potential strategic organizational security risk and developing robust mitigation controls, policies, procedures, and guidance in accordance with a developed and coherent protection and resilience strategy.

The role will work across all C&W departments across the Americas and therefore senior stakeholder engagement will be critical to the candidate’s success. The candidate must have demonstrable experience in developing senior stakeholder relationships and influencing change and improvement. As a minimum, the candidate will therefore require a proven track record in effective protection risk management and operational resilience management to be successful.

Critical elements to the role will include:

  • Foster and maintain relationships with key service line and geographical stakeholders across North America as well as Central and South America; a critical aspect of these relationships will be advising and supporting senior stakeholders in understanding and managing critical and at times complex ER&P matters, including crisis events as and when these may arise

  • Supporting C&W’s travel protection management program and partner organizations e.g., International SOS.

  • Overseeing Protection controls for Category 1 locations in region, ensuring physical protection practices and technology are fully operational, and supporting the executive protection program within Region.

  • In accordance with a defined Resilience & Protection strategy at regional level, implementing regional performance improvement initiatives to raise awareness and improve operational outcomes.

  • Managing crisis management and resilience programs to policy at a regional level for interpretation and use locally by operational businesses across the Americas.

  • Act as a trusted advisor to senior leaders within the Americas region when CMT is activated, with a permanent position on the North America, Central and Southern America Crisis Management Team(s).

  • Canning for new related legislation and working with local operational business to interpret requirements and meet legal compliance.

  • Identifying and assessing new and emerging geo-political organizational threats as they arise and taking action to support the business to mitigate strategic risks.

  • Acting as a regional ambassador for resilience & protection, implementing templates, policies, and support materials for use by the operational business and providing support as required to implement.

  • Representing C&W as required in relation to client audits, meetings, and presentations to provide assurances of C&W’s focus on regional resilience & protection.

The candidate will lead and champion the ongoing improvement of C&W’s Resilience & Protection management systems, ensuring that these align to International Standards as applicable. The candidate should have an exceptional understanding of what ‘best practice’ looks like with a clear vision of how to lead the regional organization to this goal.

The role will concentrate on physical protection risks (as opposed to data / IT protection) but will be capable of consulting with professionals in other departments to deliver a holistic resilience & protection management approach.

The role will need to co-ordinate the activities of ER&P resources around the region to effectively deliver relevant strategic initiatives including crisis management planning and exercising regimes. jobs.excerpt: Job Description: Member Solutions Group · Hiring Account Manager (Level 1)You are the person a martial-arts school owner, a fitness studio operator, or a specialty-shop merchant thinks of when they think of Member Solutions.
jobs.description:
Job Description:

Member Solutions Group · Hiring

Account Manager (Level 1)

You are the person a martial-arts school owner, a fitness studio operator, or a specialty-shop merchant thinks of when they think of Member Solutions. Not the platform, not the support line —you.

Reports toChief Growth OfficerTypeFull-time, remote-friendlyCompensation$55,000 USD base — whole comp. Standard company bonus applies separately.
The first 90 days are a pure trial.Pass/fail on measurable client-happiness signals. See "The 90-day trial" below.

The role in one paragraph

You are the person a martial-arts school owner, a fitness studio operator, or a specialty-shop merchant thinks of when they think of Member Solutions. Not the platform, not the support line —you. Your job is to make sure every client interaction feels professional, timely, and reliable, and to keep the top ~100 accounts by billing volume feeling like they are being actively cared for, with genuine understanding of their operations and challenges. You'll own the account-management motion across a book of ~500 clients, drive a small number of specific cross-team processes to completion end-to-end, and build the operational muscle — with AI leverage — that lets one person cover this current book size. Growth beyond it would justify additional hires.

Primary focus

Client happiness — four pillars

Client happiness is the whole point of this role. It gets delivered throughfour simultaneous, non-negotiable pillars:

1. Responsiveness

Inbound signal caught same-day. Hard problems have clear written expectations to resolution within 24 hours.

2. Effective problem-solving

The client's need flows end-to-end across every team it touches, or it gets handed off cleanly with the client knowing exactly what happens next. Loops close in writing. Hot potatoes escalate fast.

3. Building a self-healing MCP brain

Every recurring client question, every repeated process step, every cross-team seam-break gets captured into a shared knowledge base and evolved into an MCP or automation where it moves the metric. You are the primary input to this brain and its steward. This is how one person handles a book of 500 clients.

4. Bridging service and software

You're fluent in both — the client's operations and MSI's platform — and translating between them is core to the job. This runs in two directions. When a client's need can be solved in the software today, you show them, with real coaching. When it can't yet, you gather the evidence (which clients, what pain, what dollar value at risk) and route it to R&D through the RCB pipeline. And when something you're doing outside the platform is really working — a report clients keep asking for, a workflow that consistently delights, an insight that changes their behavior — you flag it:"should this exist in the platform?"MSI's not looking to bloat the product. The answer is yes when four things hold: multiple clients respond to it (not one), the dollar value is real (retention protected or expansion unlocked), the pattern is good enough that if it already existed in the platform and were removed the phone would ring off the hook, and keeping it in AI/service tooling long-term would cost or fail more than graduating it. When all four hold, you're the one who saw it first, and you route it to R&D the same way you'd route a Retention-Critical Bug. You are the mechanism that turns real client frictionand real client delightinto either a solved problem now or a shipped product improvement soon.

Scope

Book size and scope

  • ~500 clients totalunder this role's coverage
  • ~100 high-touch accounts(roughly the top 20% by billing volume, driving roughly 80% of the revenue) — known individually, proactive contact cadence, value reports matched to each client's need (weekly to quarterly)
  • ~400 mid-tier and long-tail accounts— the standard-service tier. Rarely touched by you directly, and often never — most self-serve through the platform and MegaMind, and they don't hit the complex or costly situations larger clients encounter. That's a healthy outcome, not neglect. Where the role compounds: AI-driven, semi-personal outreach to surface silent-but-appreciative clients who'd value a person-to-person conversation and who might have hidden or unrealized need — without ever having asked for one. You identify the pattern, help shape the outreach, and take the connections that come back — turning silence-that-isn't-a-signal into a targeted opportunity.
  • Member Solutions only.APS-system full-service billing clients. eFit is served by a separate account manager.
What you own

1Your book of ~500 clients

The ~100 high-touch names are known by heart. The rest known by tier and common concern.

2The seam between client need and MSI's ability to deliver

You own theseambetween CXSM and every other function that produces client value — Finance, R&D, CSI Pay, Product, and MSI's own AI-built tooling. This runs in two shapes.

For cross-team processes(bank account change, new account, business transfer, and any that emerge)

  • Connecting:the client's need flows end-to-end and never stalls waiting for someone to notice it
  • Awareness:CXSM knows which other-team processes exist, when they trigger, what they need as input
  • Feedback upstream:when the underlying process is breaking CX, you notify the actual process owner with a specific, evidence-backed observation — not a complaint
  • Chasing unclear questions to resolved:cross-team ambiguity doesn't die in a Teams DM

For client-facing artifacts(reports, dashboards, outputs, insights)

  • Know what exists:which reports, dashboards, and outputs MSI already has, and how to retrieve them
  • Match to client:right artifact, right client, right cadence
  • Ship the stopgap:when the client needs something MSI doesn't have yet, use AI tooling to build a "good enough" version now
  • Flag for graduation:when the AI stopgap isreallyworking (all four criteria from pillar 4), route it to R&D as a "should this exist in the platform?" candidate

Outcome — for both process and artifact:every client need is handled or handed-off quickly, efficiently, and reliably.

3The MegaMind MCP knowledge base

Every reusable answer, process shortcut, and "here's how we handle X" note lands here. It serves you first — your daily work gets faster as the brain grows, because you're not answering the same question from scratch three times a week. And it serves the team — new members query MegaMind before pulling you off task, and the whole CXSM function gets faster as the brain grows.

4Outbound cadence for the top ~100

Two phases.

Phase 1 — Days 1–60

Structured discovery

You make meaningful contact with all 100 top-tier accounts at least once. Same rigor across every one. By end of day 60, you know each client by name, business, and current concerns —ANDyou know the cadence each of them actually wants. Some want weekly. Some are perfectly served by quarterly. You don't guess; you ask.

Phase 2 — Day 61 onward

Bespoke cadence and continued discovery

For the top ~100, you execute against what each client told you: a priority-ranked list drives which accounts get worked each week — at-risk signals, active concerns, and strategic weight move accounts up. The ranking + each client's discovered cadence together determine who gets attempted. No top-100 account goes silent by default, and every client is receiving the exact cadence they expect for their business — neither less nor more.

Beyond the top ~100, discovery continues into the wider ~400 book —problems first(any client raising a cancel request, rate reduction, or complaint gets pulled in immediately), thenrevenue retention next(at-risk mid-tier accounts get proactive discovery before stable long-tail ones). Same discovery approach as Phase 1, scoped by what's actually on fire and what's at stake.

What "meaningful contact" means

Not a phone call, a Teams message, or a check-in email. Meaningful contact is a real meeting that produces a documented record: current concerns clearly articulated by the client, repeated back to confirm understanding, organized so next-step expectations can be set on each item. When the client has no current concerns, meaningful contact is a structured discovery conversation exploring their current business state and what could be better — thoughtful, question-led, focused on their pain and their desired future state.

Documentation happens through MSI's internal capture tooling and templates

You'll be trained on both in your first two weeks. Both the tools and the process are evolving; you're expected to use them as designedandto actively contribute to their improvement as you find gaps.

5The weekly leading-metric report

You own a small set of measurable indicators that show whether the role is working:

Response speed on inbound

24-hour expectation-setting rate(how consistently you set clear next-step commitments within a day)

24-hour resolution rate

Backlog trend(both this week's new items and anything overdue)

Top-100 discovery completion in Phase 1 (are you working through all 100 with the same rigor); in Phase 2, bespoke-cadence adherence for the top-100 plus reactive discovery for problem-raising clients and proactive discovery for at-risk revenue

You collect them, you report them weekly, you own the trend. Specifics are defined in your first two weeks.

What you don't own

What you hand off (and to whom)

Cancellations
→Cancellor (self-serve first), then the Member Support Lead for exception handling
Transfer of ownership
→Documented workflow → CXSM specialist
Deep product support
→R&D or Product
Tough negotiations, retention save-attempts on top accounts
→Chief Growth Officer
Tooling

Tools you'll use daily

HubSpot
The CRM. Every conversation logged, every contact fresh.
Microsoft Teams
Internal comms, cross-team coordination.
Claude Desktop / Claude Code
AI assistant for drafting communications, summarizing calls, mining transcripts, running MCP tools.
ADO (Azure DevOps)
The R&D-facing surface for submitting Retention-Critical Bugs.
SharePoint
Document store, process docs.
Amazon Connect
MSI's inbound phone system. You take calls here and your response speed is measured across every channel including this one.
CallHero
The AI-scored call corpus. Use it to prep for calls, spot commitment-breaks, catch churn signals.
Cancellor
The member self-service cancellation portal. You review the escalations, not the routine cases.
MegaMind (MCP)
The internal knowledge base you feed and query.
Anny (MCP)
Analytics on client website + search performance when a client asks "how are we doing?"
APS / Cubiic
The billing and revenue-recovery systems.

You are not expected to be an engineer. You are expected to beAI-fluent — or actively becoming AI-fluent— comfortable in the tools, quick to build a shortcut with them, and willing to convert a manual process into an MCP workflow so it runs 5× faster next time. Existing proof points:/taskois a ~100× improvement over the HubSpot GUI for task triage;hubmcpis 5×+ on HubSpot company/ticket updates.

Measurement

How improvement gets measured

Leading indicators(weekly signal — you control these directly):response speed on inbound, 24-hour expectation-setting rate, 24-hour resolution rate, backlog trend (active and aged), and top-100 outreach discipline — discovery completion in Phase 1, then bespoke-cadence adherence plus reactive/proactive discovery in Phase 2. The exact metric definitions and collection method are defined in your first two weeks.

Lagging indicators(quarterly signal — the business sees these over time):CSAT trend, referral rate, retention on the top ~100.

The leading metrics cause the lagging ones. If you're executing on the leading pillars, the lagging outcomes follow. Weekly cadence for the leading metrics; quarterly review of the lagging ones.

No a-priori automation quota.When you capture a recurring pattern (three clients asking the same question this week, a cross-team workflow that keeps stalling at the same seam), it becomes an MCP or Claude-workflow candidate. CGO + AM analyze weekly with Claude — keep what moves the metric, kill what doesn't.

The trial

The 90-day trial

Pass/fail on measurable movement in the leading metrics— plus early signal that the lagging indicators are pointing the right direction.

Pass:If leading metrics move and lagging signals point right, we revisit comp and additional bonus structures at day 90.
Watch:If leading metrics move but lagging signals stay flat, we look at whether R&D is delivering on the RCB pipeline and whether the play needs adjustment upstream.
Reset:If leading metrics don't move, we revisit the whole shape.

This isn't a soft ramp. It's the gate for the role continuing.

What the first 90 days actually look like

Days 1–30 — Absorb the book, establish baseline

Sit with the CGO on top-100 accounts. Start Phase 1 discovery — meaningful contact with the highest-priority accounts first. Establish week-1 numbers on all five leading indicators — these become your baseline. Start feeding MegaMind. Weekly attempt target is set with the CGO by end of week 2 based on what you can actually sustain.

Days 31–60 — Complete Phase 1 discovery and move the leading numbers

Meaningful contact with all 100 top-tier accounts by day 60 — each of them known by name, business, current concerns, and preferred cadence. Response speed dropping, resolution rates rising, backlog trending down. Start surfacing RCB candidates through the weekly R&D triage. Reactive save-attempts landing as they come in.

Days 61–90 — Enter Phase 2 and show the leading-to-lagging chain

Bespoke cadence operational for all 100 top-tier. Reactive discovery flowing into the wider ~400 book (any client raising an issue gets pulled in). First proactive discovery on at-risk mid-tier accounts. First CSAT tick, first unprompted referral, first save that would have been a churn —a client writing a positive review unprompted is the visible signal. MegaMind has demonstrably grown; other CXSM members are using entries you've fed.

Fit

Who succeeds — and who will struggle

Who succeeds

  • Relentless aboutclosing loops in writing.Every conversation ends with "here's what happens next, by when, from whom."
  • Allergic to letting accounts drift silently.You know each top-100 client's rhythm — some weekly, some monthly, some quarterly — and you notice the moment one falls out of their rhythm.
  • Believes process documentation is not bureaucracy — it's how you sleep at night and how the team scales.
  • AI-fluent or actively becoming AI-fluent.Uses Claude Desktop daily. Knows HubSpot. Learns MCP tooling.
  • Humble about hot potatoes— escalates fast, doesn't hero-mode.
  • Can hold ~100 top-tier accounts in your head without dropping any, and triage the other ~400 by pattern.
  • Comfortable withmassive hands-on work.This is a doer role, not a manager role. Every day is real client issues, real process work.

Who will struggle

  • Needs a rigid process before starting — this role helps build the process.
  • Uncomfortable with repetitive work — some days you run the same three workflows 40 times.
  • Hides from hard conversations. This jobisthe hard conversation.
  • Not curious about AI. The efficiency gains that make this book size survivable aren't optional.
The company

About Member Solutions

Member Solutions is a 35-year-old billing platform serving martial arts schools, fitness studios, and specialty member-based businesses. A longtime client recently described MSI as"a Titan of the industry in 2015."We're rebuilding to be worthy of that description again. This role is a critical part of that.

Competencies

Competencies we're hiring for

Framed against the Lominger Standard 67 Competency framework. These are the six that map most tightly to how this role actually succeeds. If you recognize yourself in most of them, we should talk.

1. Customer FocusLominger #15

The whole point of the role. Not just supporting customers — dedicated to their expectations and requirements, gets first-hand customer information, uses it for improvements in products and services, acts with customers in mind, establishes and maintains effective relationships with customers, gains their trust and respect.

2. Action OrientedLominger #1

Enjoys working hard; action oriented and full of energy for the things seen as challenging; not fearful of acting with a minimum of planning; seizes more opportunities than others. This is a doer role, not a manager role. Every day is real client issues, real process work.

3. Process ManagementLominger #52

Good at figuring out the processes necessary to get things done; knows how to organize people and activities; understands how to separate and combine tasks into efficient workflow; knows what to measure and how to measure it; can simplify complex processes; gets more out of fewer resources. The whole one-person-covering-500-clients thesis depends on this.

4. Interpersonal SavvyLominger #31

Relates well to all kinds of people, up, down, and sideways, inside and outside the organization; builds appropriate rapport; builds constructive and effective relationships; uses diplomacy and tact; can diffuse even high-tension situations comfortably.

5. Drive For ResultsLominger #53

Can be counted on to exceed goals successfully; is constantly and consistently one of the top performers; very bottom-line oriented; steadfastly pushes self and others for results. The 90-day pass/fail trial and the "100 top-tier connected by day 60" milestone both live here.

6. Learning on the FlyLominger #32

Learns quickly when facing new problems; a relentless and versatile learner; open to change; analyzes both successes and failures for clues to improvement; experiments and will try anything to find solutions; enjoys the challenge of unfamiliar tasks; quickly grasps the essence and the underlying structure of anything. Position Overview

The Communications Manager is responsible for managing the Foundation's communications and digital presence across multiple audiences, programmes, and campaigns. This role goes beyond social media execution by leading creative production, coordinating external creative partners, managing content workflows, and ensuring all communications are delivered on time, on brand, and aligned with organizational priorities. Working closely with leadership, programme teams, fundraising, and external vendors, the Communications Manager serves as the central point of coordination for communications projects from concept through publication.

Key Responsibilities

  • Oversee content planning and publishing across Instagram, LinkedIn, Facebook, YouTube, and other relevant platforms.
  • Coordinate campaigns across multiple Foundation and programme social media handles.

Organizational Communications & Website Management

  • Coordinate communications materials supporting fundraising campaigns, grant announcements, partnerships, events, programme launches, and organizational updates.
  • Co-manage the Foundation's website with the Director of Operations, ensuring content remains current, accurate, and aligned with organizational priorities.

  • Work with external web developers and designers to implement new pages, functionality, and improvements.

  • Monitor website performance and user experience, identifying opportunities to improve engagement and accessibility.
  • Support the creation of presentations, newsletters, digital reports, and other marketing and communications collateral as needed.

Engagement & Community Management

  • Monitor audience responses, mentions, and direct messages across platforms.
  • Coordinate with internal teams to ensure timely and appropriate responses.
  • Identify opportunities to amplify partner content or mission-aligned news.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Partner with programme, fundraising, operations, and leadership teams to identify communications needs and priorities.
  • Ensure timely collection of content, photography, success stories, and programme updates.
  • Keep communications projects moving by proactively managing timelines, dependencies, and deliverables.

Analytics & Continuous Improvement

  • Monitor platform performance and campaign effectiveness.
  • Prepare concise monthly reports highlighting engagement, growth, campaign performance, and recommendations.
  • Recommend improvements based on analytics, audience trends, and organizational priorities.

Tools & Platforms

  • Asana, HubSpot, Canva Pro, Google Drive, Hootsuite, Instagram, LinkedIn, YouTube, TikTok, . Adobe Suite experience a plus!

Qualifications

  • 5+ years of experience in communications, social media, or digital marketing, preferably within a nonprofit or mission-driven organization.
  • Demonstrated experience managing communications projects from planning through execution.
  • Experience coordinating and managing external creative vendors, including designers, photographers, videographers, and editors.
  • Excellent copywriting and editing skills with strong attention to detail.
  • Ability to provide concise, constructive, and actionable creative feedback.
  • Strong project management and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple concurrent priorities.
  • Experience developing communications calendars and coordinating cross-functional teams.
  • Proficiency with Asana, HubSpot, Canva Pro, Google Workspace, Frame.io, and social media management platforms.
  • Self-directed, highly organized, and comfortable working in a fast-paced, remote environment.
  • Passion for the Foundation's mission and global impact.

Compensation & Hours

  • $25-$30/hour depending on experience
  • Approximately 10–15 hours per week, with flexibility during major campaigns.
  • Independent contractor position with performance reviews at 3 and 6 months.

Benefits

  • Flexible remote work environment.
  • Opportunity to lead communications for a growing global nonprofit.
  • Collaborative, mission-driven team with meaningful international impact.

Application Instructions

Please submit your resume, portfolio or examples of relevant communications work, and a brief cover letter describing your experience managing communications campaigns and creative projects. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled.

We are seeking candidates who bring a deep contextual understanding of Africa and a strong alignment with our mission and values. This may come through lived experience, long-term professional engagement, or meaningful personal connection to the regions and communities we serve. Our work is rooted in respect for local leadership, cultural knowledge, and community-driven solutions, and we prioritize applicants who demonstrate humility, accountability, and a clear commitment to working in partnership with diverse stakeholders.

The Elba Hope Foundation is an Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected characteristic.

Every year, we sponsor 2 remote UX apprentices from anywhere in the world to join us for 7 months, either in the fall or spring seasons or online. We are committed to helping women, immigrants, POC, and LGBTQ folks break into tech and land 6-figure UX jobs. We help you land 6-figure UX jobs or coach you till you get it.

Apprenticeship Requirements:

This apprenticeship program is open to new grads and UX career changers alike! Here are some apprenticeship requirements to keep in mind before applying:
Interested in creative tech career paths in UX research, UX design, product design or service design
Willing to commit 5-10 hours of work per week to complete program deliverables
Willing to attend 2-3 hour weekend lectures to learn the end-to-end design process OR willing to complete online video course modules
Open to feedback from UX mentors and demonstrates a willingness to revise design work

Build digital products and services 0-1

Develop a business model for the product or service and demonstrate how the product/service will scale as the business model scales

Position Type: Full-Time, Remote
Location: Remote (must have real-time overlap with U.S. Eastern business hours)
Reports To: CEO

About the Role

At Pavago, one of our clients is hiring an experienced Sales Manager to lead and coach a team of Outside Sales Representatives (OSRs) through the complete B2B sales cycle.

This is not an SDR management role.

Instead of focusing solely on prospecting activity, you’ll own the entire sales motion—from pipeline generation and discovery through presentations, negotiations, closing, and account development—while coaching your team to consistently improve performance.

We’re looking for a leader who has personally carried a quota, built pipeline, closed deals, and understands what it takes to succeed in consultative B2B sales. If you’ve successfully transitioned from top-performing salesperson to hands-on sales leader and enjoy developing high-performing teams, this role is an excellent fit.

What You’ll Own

Full-Cycle Sales Leadership

  • Lead and coach Outside Sales Representatives across the complete sales cycle.
  • Support reps through:
    • Prospecting
    • Pipeline generation
    • Qualification
    • Discovery
    • Solution presentations
    • Objection handling
    • Negotiation
    • Closing
    • Account nurturing
  • Drive consistent execution of the sales process while improving win rates and sales effectiveness.

Sales Coaching & Team Development

  • Coach both experienced and junior sales representatives.
  • Conduct live coaching sessions during customer calls.
  • Review recorded calls and provide actionable feedback.
  • Help reps improve discovery, positioning, negotiation, and closing skills.
  • Build a culture of continuous learning and accountability.

Sales Process & Playbook Development

  • Develop, refine, and document scalable sales processes.
  • Create structured playbooks, coaching guides, and best practices.
  • Standardize sales methodologies across the team.
  • Continuously improve workflows based on performance data and market feedback.

AI-Driven Sales Management

  • Leverage AI tools to improve coaching, sales execution, and operational efficiency.
  • Build and manage workflows using tools such as:
    • Claude Projects
    • Claude Code
    • Claude Cowork
  • Analyze sales calls, pipeline data, and team performance using AI.
  • Use AI to create and continuously improve sales documentation and playbooks.

Pipeline & Performance Management

  • Monitor pipeline health and forecasting accuracy.
  • Conduct pipeline reviews and deal strategy sessions.
  • Identify risks, bottlenecks, and opportunities.
  • Ensure CRM data remains accurate and up to date.
  • Track key sales metrics and coach toward continuous improvement.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Partner with leadership to align sales strategy and business goals.
  • Share customer feedback and market insights with internal teams.
  • Support ongoing improvements to messaging, positioning, and sales enablement.

Requirements

Must-Have Qualifications

Experience

  • Proven experience managing full-cycle B2B sales teams.
  • Demonstrated success leading Outside Sales Representatives—not just SDR or appointment-setting teams.
  • Personal experience carrying a sales quota and closing complex B2B deals.
  • Experience generating your own pipeline, running discovery calls, presenting solutions, negotiating, and closing business.

Industry Knowledge

  • Strong background in Managed Service Providers (MSP) or IT Services is highly preferred.
  • Solid understanding of consultative technology sales processes.

AI & Technology

  • Hands-on experience using AI tools within daily sales operations.
  • Comfortable working with:
    • Claude Projects
    • Claude Code
    • Claude Cowork
  • Ability to use AI for:
    • Sales coaching
    • Pipeline analysis
    • Playbook creation
    • Process optimization

Leadership & Communication

  • Strong coaching, mentoring, and leadership abilities.
  • Experience writing and improving sales playbooks and processes.
  • Excellent verbal and written English communication skills.
  • Native or near-native English proficiency strongly preferred.
  • Availability to work during U.S. Eastern business hours.

Nice-to-Have

  • Experience selling or managing sales teams within:
    • Managed IT Services
    • Cybersecurity
    • Cloud Solutions
    • Professional Services
  • Experience building high-performing remote sales teams.
  • Familiarity with modern CRM platforms and sales analytics tools.
  • Experience implementing AI-driven sales enablement strategies.

What Makes You a Strong Fit

  • Proven full-cycle B2B sales leader.
  • Strong consultative selling mindset.
  • Excellent coach who develops people through structured feedback.
  • Process-oriented while remaining adaptable.
  • Comfortable balancing live coaching with asynchronous development.
  • Curious, technology-driven, and enthusiastic about AI.
  • High ownership, accountability, and continuous improvement mindset.

What a Typical Day Looks Like

  • Review pipeline health and forecast opportunities.
  • Conduct live coaching sessions with sales representatives.
  • Join discovery calls and deal strategy discussions.
  • Review recorded sales calls and provide coaching.
  • Develop and improve sales playbooks using AI tools.
  • Analyze sales metrics and identify coaching opportunities.
  • Collaborate with leadership on sales strategy and process improvements.

In short: You build high-performing sales professionals by coaching every stage of the sales cycle while continuously improving the team’s processes, tools, and performance.

Key Metrics for Success (KPIs)

  • Team quota attainment.
  • Pipeline growth and health.
  • Opportunity-to-close conversion rate.
  • Sales cycle efficiency.
  • Forecast accuracy.
  • CRM hygiene and pipeline management.
  • Rep development and coaching effectiveness.
  • Adoption of sales processes and playbooks.

Why Join Us?

  • Lead a full-cycle B2B sales organization.
  • Work directly with executive leadership.
  • High ownership over sales performance and coaching.
  • Opportunity to shape sales processes using modern AI tools.
  • Fully remote work environment with real business impact.
  • Clear growth path into:
    • Director of Sales
    • Head of Sales
    • VP of Sales
    • Revenue Leadership

Interview Process

  1. Initial Phone Screen
  2. Spark Hire Intro Video (3–5 minutes)
  3. Sales Leadership & Coaching Interview
  4. Client Interview with CEO
  5. Offer & Onboarding

What Happens After You Apply

Right after you apply, you’ll receive an email invitation from Spark Hire to record your Intro Video. This short, self-recorded video is the next step that completes your application and can be recorded whenever it’s convenient for you.

Instead of repeating yourself across multiple screening calls, you’ll introduce yourself once, and your video will be shared with the hiring team. This helps the hiring team evaluate your communication style early, making future interviews more meaningful while reducing unnecessary interview rounds.

Don’t overthink it—you can record your video as many times as you’d like before submitting it. Only your final submission will be reviewed.

Please keep an eye on both your inbox and spam folder for your Spark Hire invitation after submitting your application.

Apply Now

If you’re an experienced Sales Manager who has successfully led full-cycle B2B sales teams, thrives on coaching consultative selling, embraces AI-powered sales management, and wants to help build a high-performing sales organization, we’d love to hear from you. Apply today and play a key role in driving revenue growth while developing the next generation of top-performing sales professionals.

jobs.title: Sr Red Hat/UniVerse Administrator
jobs.excerpt: Hajoca Corporation is one of the country’s largest privately-held wholesale distributors of plumbing, heating & cooling, and industrial supplies.
jobs.description:
Hajoca Corporation is one of the country’s largest privately-held wholesale distributors of plumbing, heating & cooling, and industrial supplies. Founded in 1858, Hajoca is a company based on the principles of “Service, Integrity, Reliability,” and on relationships of trust and support with teammates, customers, and suppliers. Throughout its history, Hajoca has played an active role in shaping advances in plumbing. However, we attribute our success to two simple truths; a unique business philosophy and talented people. Hajoca is all about the people, who give us our advantage, and who will guide us successfully into the future.

Hajoca has over 400 locations nationwide, called Profit Centers; and at the foundation of our family of businesses is a National Support Center (NSC) where Centers of Excellence are dedicated to enabling the success of our Profit Centers.

The Infrastructure Operations team in our National Support Center (NSC) is looking for a Sr Red Hat/UniVerse Administrator at their Lafayette Hill, PA office. This position is remote.

Do you have deep, hands-on experience administering Red Hat Enterprise Linux and Rocket UniVerse or another MultiValue database? Do you enjoy tuning, securing, and troubleshooting the infrastructure supporting a mission-critical ERP platform? Are you excited by the opportunity to own the SQL replication pipeline connecting Eclipse operational data to enterprise reporting and analytics? If so, then we’d like you to join our dedicated team as a Senior Red Hat / UniVerse Administrator.

About the Role:

The Senior Red Hat / UniVerse Administrator is the senior technical owner of the platform that Hajoca’s Epicor Eclipse ERP runs on — the Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) operating environment, the Rocket UniVerse MultiValue database beneath Eclipse, and the near real time SQL replication layer that feeds the enterprise data warehouse and business intelligence. This role keeps a mission critical, 24×7 distribution platform stable, secure, high performing, and highly available across production and non production environments, while ensuring that operational Eclipse data flows accurately and continuously into SQL Server for reporting and analytics.

The ideal candidate blends deep Linux systems administration with hands on MultiValue database expertise and a strong data integration mindset — someone who can tune the OS and the UniVerse database, work fluently within the Eclipse ecosystem, and own the replication pipeline that turns nested MultiValue records into clean relational data for Power BI, SSRS, and Excel.

In this role, you will:

Own Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) Administration

  • Install, configure, patch, and upgrade RHEL servers (physical and virtual) that host the Eclipse/UniVerse environment, keeping the estate on current, supported releases.
  • Tune the kernel, filesystems (LVM/XFS), memory, and CPU for MultiValue database workloads and heavy transactional I/O.
  • Automate provisioning, patching, and configuration management with Red Hat Satellite and Bash scripting to drive consistency and reduce manual effort.
  • Monitor system health, forecast capacity, and proactively tune performance to sustain availability targets.
  • Administer users, groups, permissions, SSH, sudo/PAM, and OS hardening in line with security policy.
  • Manage, networking (interface bonding, firewalld, DNS, NTP), systemd services, logging, and scheduled jobs.

Own Rocket UniVerse / MultiValue Database Administration

  • Administer Rocket UniVerse (U2) MultiValue database instances underpinning Epicor Eclipse — including accounts, files, file sizing/resizing, hashing, and record/group locks.
  • Diagnose and resolve locking, contention, and session issues; tune uvconfig, phantom processes, and shared memory parameters for optimal throughput.
  • Perform backups, transaction logging, and point in time recovery; validate restore procedures on a regular cadence.
  • Apply MultiValue performance monitoring (e.g., Rocket MVX: Performance) to track sessions, locks, host resources, and replication health.
  • Use RetrieVe/UniQuery and read UniVerse BASIC to investigate data issues and support reporting.
  • Maintain UniVerse licensing, TLS transport encryption, and data at rest encryption; open and manage support cases with Rocket Software or the VAR.

Own Epicor Eclipse SQL Replication & Maintain the Data Warehouse

  • Own the Epicor Eclipse SQL Replication engine that provides near real time replication of core Eclipse UniVerse (MultiValue) database files directly into a structured SQL Server data warehouse environment.
  • Configure, schedule, and continuously monitor replication so operational transactional data syncs into SQL tables with acceptable latency and completeness.
  • Manage the mapping and transformation that flattens nested multi value fields — such as multiple order lines within a single record — into standard relational rows and columns.
  • Administer the Information Control Engine (ICE) integration that feeds Eclipse data into dashboards and BI.
  • Maintain the SQL Server data warehouse (schema, indexing, SQL Agent jobs, and storage) and preserve a clean, standard schema for third party reporting.
  • Enable and support downstream reporting connections — Power BI, SSRS, and Excel — offloading heavy queries from the primary Eclipse environment to protect production performance.
  • Detect and resolve replication failures, resync/backfill gaps, and continuously verify data integrity between Eclipse and the SQL targets.

Ensure Backup, Disaster Recovery & High Availability

  • Design, execute, and document backup and recovery strategies spanning RHEL, UniVerse, Eclipse, and the SQL data warehouse.
  • Own disaster recovery planning and regular failover/recovery testing to meet defined RTO/RPO objectives.
  • Ensure business continuity for a 24×7 distribution operation, including participation in an on call rotation.

Govern Security & Compliance

  • Harden and patch RHEL against recognized benchmarks (e.g., CIS / DISA STIG) and manage vulnerability remediation.
  • Enforce least privilege access, audit logging, and change management discipline across the platform stack.
  • Support enterprise security and compliance initiatives in partnership with the Cyber Security & AI Enablement team.

Drive Automation, Documentation & Collaboration

  • Build and maintain automation (Ansible playbooks and scripts) for repeatable, auditable operations.
  • Produce and maintain runbooks, SOPs, architecture diagrams, and knowledge base articles.
  • Partner across Infrastructure, Applications & Support, Networking, and Cyber teams, and with business stakeholders.
  • Mentor junior administrators and actively share scarce MultiValue/Eclipse knowledge across the team.

About You:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • 7+ years of progressive systems administration experience, including some senior level ownership of production environments.
  • Preferred Certifications include Red Hat Certified System Administrator (RHCSA) and/or Red Hat Certified Engineer (RHCE), Rocket U2 (UniVerse / UniData) training or certification, Microsoft SQL Server certification (e.g., Azure Database Administrator Associate).

Our ideal candidate will also:

  • Have deep, hands on Red Hat Enterprise Linux administration experience— installation, patching, performance tuning, storage, networking, and security.
  • Have hands on experience administering a MultiValue database — Rocket UniVerse or UniData (U2), or another Pick based platform.
  • Possess a working knowledge of Epicor Eclipse ERP (or a comparable MultiValue based distribution ERP) sufficient to support the underlying database and data pipeline — Eclipse application administration is owned by a separate partner role.
  • Possess a working knowledge of Microsoft SQL Server and of data replication / ETL concepts.
  • Be proficient in Bash scripting and automation with Ansible.
  • Possess strong analytical and troubleshooting skills and the ability to react quickly and decisively during incidents.
  • Have virtualization (VMware) and enterprise storage (SAN/NAS) experience.
  • Be available for after hours maintenance windows and shared on call support.
  • Have direct experience with Epicor Eclipse SQL Replication and the Information Control Engine (ICE).
  • Possess reporting/BI integration experience with Power BI, SSRS, and Excel against a replicated SQL data warehouse.
  • Have a background in wholesale distribution or another multi site, high transaction environment. a background in wholesale distribution or another multi site, high transaction environment.
  • Be familiar with UniVerse BASIC and comfortable reading and adjusting existing MultiValue code.
  • Have experience coordinating vendor support relationships (Epicor, Rocket Software, and VARs).
  • Have experience with Rubrik Data Protection for management of backups, recovery, and vulnerability scanning.
  • Have experience with Zerto Continuous Data Protection.
  • Demonstrate strong functional knowledge; take ownership of skills, knowledge, and relationships needed to perform the job.
  • Be professional, organized, and able to manage work, time, and problems.
  • Be results oriented; focused on attaining goals and objectives.
  • Have a keen ability to interpret technical problems and systematically troubleshoot and resolve.

The benefits of working with us:

Our culture is well-suited for exceptional people who use their talents to drive business and want to share in the financial success their efforts yield. In addition to a competitive starting wage, we offer a Profit-Sharing Program that provides each team member with an opportunity to earn a direct share of the profits on an annual basis.   • Medical, dental, vision, and prescription coverage

  • Pre-tax accounts for healthcare, dependent care, and commuter benefits
  • Paid vacation, holidays, and sick time (sick time also offered to PT team members as required by state law)

  • You default to ownership; if it falls between roles, you pick it up.

Business Development Representative (BDR) – Outbound Sales & Lead Generation

Position Type: Full-Time, Remote
Working Hours: U.S. Business Hours

About the Role

We’re hiring a results-driven Business Development Representative (BDR) to generate qualified sales opportunities through outbound prospecting, lead qualification, discovery calls, and pipeline development.

You’ll be responsible for identifying potential customers, reaching decision-makers, understanding their business needs, and converting conversations into qualified meetings for Account Executives.

This is an ideal opportunity for someone who enjoys B2B sales, cold calling, outbound outreach, relationship building, and creating pipeline in a fast-paced, performance-driven environment.

What You’ll Own

Outbound Prospecting & Lead Generation

  • Research and identify target accounts and decision-makers
  • Build prospect lists using tools such as:
    • LinkedIn Sales Navigator
    • Apollo
    • ZoomInfo
    • Similar prospecting platforms
  • Execute multi-channel outreach through:
    • Cold calls
    • Email
    • LinkedIn
    • Social outreach
  • Personalize messaging based on industry, ICP, role, and business challenges
  • Maintain consistent prospecting activity and generate new pipeline

Lead Qualification & Discovery

  • Respond to and qualify inbound leads from marketing, referrals, events, and website inquiries
  • Conduct discovery and qualification calls
  • Understand prospect:
    • Business needs
    • Pain points
    • Budget
    • Timeline
    • Buying process
    • Decision-makers
  • Use qualification frameworks such as BANT, MEDDIC, SPICED, or SPIN
  • Determine sales readiness and identify high-potential opportunities

Meeting Setting & Sales Handoff

  • Schedule qualified meetings and demos for Account Executives
  • Prepare detailed qualification and discovery notes
  • Ensure Account Executives have the context needed for productive sales conversations
  • Coordinate follow-ups and next steps
  • Maintain a smooth prospect experience throughout the handoff

Pipeline Nurturing

  • Follow up consistently with early-stage prospects
  • Re-engage inactive or previously interested leads
  • Build relationships through consultative communication
  • Share relevant resources, case studies, and information
  • Maintain organized follow-up sequences so opportunities don’t fall through the cracks

CRM & Pipeline Management

  • Maintain accurate CRM records using platforms such as:
    • Salesforce
    • HubSpot
    • Zoho CRM
  • Track calls, emails, meetings, notes, and follow-up activity
  • Update lead stages and opportunity status
  • Maintain strong CRM hygiene and documentation
  • Track pipeline generation and conversion metrics

Sales & Marketing Collaboration

  • Work closely with Account Executives and sales leadership
  • Share prospect feedback, objections, and market insights
  • Collaborate with marketing to improve targeting and messaging
  • Participate in pipeline reviews and sales strategy discussions
  • Test and improve outreach messaging based on performance

What Makes You a Strong Fit

  • You’re confident picking up the phone and starting conversations
  • You enjoy outbound prospecting and building pipeline
  • You can qualify prospects without making conversations feel scripted
  • You’re persuasive, consultative, and a strong listener
  • You stay organized across large numbers of prospects and follow-ups
  • You’re resilient and comfortable working toward measurable targets
  • You take feedback well and continuously improve your approach

Required Experience & Skills

  • 2+ years of experience in:
    • Business Development
    • Sales Development
    • Inside Sales
    • Outbound Prospecting
  • Proven experience with cold calling and outbound lead generation
  • Experience conducting discovery and qualification calls
  • Strong written and verbal English communication skills
  • Hands-on CRM experience with Salesforce, HubSpot, Zoho, or similar
  • Experience with prospecting or sales engagement tools such as:
    • LinkedIn Sales Navigator
    • Apollo
    • Outreach
    • Salesloft
    • ZoomInfo
  • Strong follow-up and pipeline management skills
  • Ability to work independently during U.S. business hours

Nice to Have

  • 3–5 years of BDR/SDR experience with demonstrated quota attainment
  • Experience selling:
    • B2B SaaS
    • Technology solutions
    • Professional services
    • High-ticket products or services
  • Experience supporting mid-market or enterprise sales
  • Familiarity with:
    • MEDDIC
    • SPIN Selling
    • Challenger Sale
    • Sandler
  • Account-based prospecting experience
  • Experience running multi-channel outbound sequences

What a Typical Day Looks Like

You may start by reviewing your pipeline and prioritizing follow-ups before building a new list of target accounts and decision-makers.

Throughout the day, you’ll make outbound calls, send personalized emails and LinkedIn messages, respond to inbound leads, conduct discovery conversations, and schedule qualified meetings for Account Executives.

You’ll document activity in the CRM, coordinate handoffs, review outreach performance, and refine your messaging based on what’s generating conversations.

In short: you create new sales opportunities by finding the right prospects, starting meaningful conversations, qualifying their needs, and moving strong opportunities into the sales pipeline.

Key Metrics for Success

  • Qualified opportunities generated
  • Meetings and discovery calls booked
  • Outbound calls, emails, and LinkedIn activity
  • Lead-to-opportunity conversion rate
  • Pipeline value generated
  • Outbound response and engagement rates
  • Meeting show rate
  • CRM accuracy and follow-up consistency
  • Achievement of monthly and quarterly targets

Why This Role Stands Out

  • Direct impact on pipeline and company revenue
  • Hands-on experience with modern B2B prospecting tools
  • Work closely with Account Executives and sales leadership
  • Develop advanced discovery, qualification, and outbound sales skills
  • Fully remote environment aligned with U.S. business hours
  • Clear career progression into:
    • Senior BDR / SDR
    • Account Executive
    • Business Development Manager
    • Sales Leadership

Interview Process

  1. Initial Application Review
  2. Intro Video via Spark Hire
  3. Practical Assessment – Mock Discovery Call / Qualification Exercise
  4. Client Interview
  5. Offer & Onboarding

What Happens After You Apply

Right after you apply, you’ll receive an email invitation from Spark Hire to record your Intro Video. It’s a short, self-recorded video completed on your own time and is the final step needed to complete your application.

Instead of repeating your background across multiple screening calls, you get to introduce yourself once and show hiring teams how you communicate before the first interview. If there’s a strong fit, your first live conversation can focus on the opportunity rather than starting from scratch.

Don’t overthink it. You can record your responses multiple times, and discarded takes are not shared.

Please keep an eye on both your inbox and spam folder for the Spark Hire invitation.

Apply Now

If you:

  • Have experience in BDR, SDR, or outbound sales
  • Are confident with cold calling and prospecting
  • Know how to qualify prospects and book strong meetings
  • Enjoy building relationships and creating new opportunities
  • Thrive in a metrics-driven B2B sales environment

We’d love to hear from you.

jobs.description:
AIT is the world's largest provider of automation, factory integration and tooling solutions dedicated to the global aerospace, defense, and space launch vehicle industries.

AIT offers a competitive compensation package (including free medical options for employees and their family), casual work environment and excellent growth opportunities.

This is a Remote position which requires 100% travel.

Summary:

The Electrician and Controls Field Engineer is responsible for the installation, maintenance, and repair of electrical wiring, electrical panels, equipment, and fixtures. Additionally, they will assist in the troubleshooting of PLC’s, HMI’s and numerical control interfaces.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Accountable for comprehensive heavy duty electrical installations, encompassing the connection from the factory input source, the initialization of equipment, and the wiring of control panels.
  • Executes tasks that demand a deep understanding of electrical and electronic theories and principles, mechanical principles, written specifications, local and national electrical codes, material properties, and the operational principles and applications of electronic equipment.
  • Receive wiring diagrams, drawings, specifications, and instructions, whether conveyed verbally or in written form, regarding both emergency and scheduled repair, installation, and inspection tasks to be executed.
  • Initiates equipment start-up and shutdown procedures in strict adherence to operational needs, company safety protocols, and compliance with OSHA regulations governing machine activation and deactivation.
  • Attains expertise in operating site-specific automation system software and technology, which includes alignment systems, AGVs, heating solutions, and more.
  • Provides technical support for operational needs related to PLCs, HMIs, and network interfaces.
  • Performs installation, troubleshooting, and maintenance of mechanical, hydraulic, pneumatic, electrical, and electronic equipment, encompassing PLCs, HMIs, numerical controls, power supplies, drives, gauges, and test equipment.
  • Services electronic equipment through the inspection, testing, and replacement of malfunctioning components, circuit modules, printed circuit boards, fuses, and other related electronic devices.
  • Maintains the installation and upkeep of communication cables, power distribution cables, and wiring, including performing necessary splicing tasks as needed.
  • Develops detailed working procedures to assess material requirements or replacements and establishes a logical approach to resolve repair issues.
  • Formulates a concise and comprehensive tie-in that outlines encountered issues, details troubleshooting procedures undertaken, corrective measures implemented, identifies the root cause, and delineates future actions.
  • Maintains and generates documentation essential for training and knowledge dissemination related to the supported control systems.
  • Collaborates with and provides assistance to fellow engineering colleagues involved in complementary electrical hardware engineering tasks.
  • Advocates for and adheres to sound safety practices and habits, including but not limited to the proper utilization of all required personal protective equipment (PPE).
  • Executes all responsibilities in a safe and cooperative manner and promptly notifies the supervisor of any potentially hazardous conditions or other safety-related concerns.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

List of needed knowledge, skills, and abilities to successfully accomplish the duties and responsibilities of the job.

  • Deep understanding of electrical principles, voltage, current, resistance, and Ohm's law, is essential.
  • Professional understanding of blueprints, schematics, and/or measuring devices.
  • Must have a fundamental understanding of PLC controlled systems, HMI configuration and programming Control circuit analysis and hardware.
  • Mandatory involvement in all stages of the product lifecycle, encompassing electrical and hardware aspects, control system installation, rigorous testing, start-up procedures, and thorough debugging. Additionally, providing assistance to fellow engineering colleagues involved in electrical hardware and software engineering tasks.
  • Capable of addressing fundamental customer site requirement adjustments and assisting in delivering solutions for completion of equipment installation, start-ups, and testing as per design specifications.
  • Performs routine maintenance on equipment and determine when and types of maintenance required.
  • Demonstrates consistent and predictable behavior, characterized by reliability, responsibility, and dependability in fulfilling obligations. Maintains a strong commitment to follow through on commitments and consistently meets deadlines.
  • Demonstrates a high level of self-direction and initiative in all aspects of performance and knowledge acquisition. Proficient in problem-solving, readily addressing challenges as they arise, and actively seeking suitable solutions when personal expertise is limited.
  • Attains a high level of thoroughness and precision when completing tasks across all relevant areas.
  • Possesses clear and effective communication skills, proficient in both written and verbal formats.
  • Proficient in computer usage, including tasks like locating and opening files, navigating websites, conducting duty-related searches, and downloading files as required.
  • Familiarity with computer applications, email, databases, and spreadsheets, such as Microsoft Office.
  • Respond and follow up to a customer inquiries or problems in a timely and effective manner.
  • Identifies problems and review relevant information to develop options, then implement solutions.
  • At ease with communicating and collaborating effectively with individuals at various levels of management, fellow team members, and customers.

Education and Work Experience:

  • Must have a demonstratable track record in the role of an industrial electrician.
  • Technician Certification or Associates degree in a related field required.
  • Bachelor’s degree, PE, SSE in electrical, manufacturing, or mechanical engineering preferred but not required.
  • Minimum of two-years and/or equivalent experience preferred in PLC and HMI configuration and programming Control circuit analysis, design, troubleshooting and solving software/hardware issues in an industrial high voltage electrical maintenance.

Work Authorization/Security Clearance Requirements:

  • This position may require a government security clearance; you must be a US Citizen for consideration.
  • Must be clean of any prior felony or federal convictions.

Work Conditions:

Environment Type:

  • 90% Indoors, 10% Outdoors. Temperature controlled, unless environment conditions specify otherwise.
  • Production setting environments.
  • Heavy Industrial and Construction environments.

Exposure Types:

  • Cuts, burns and scrapes.
  • Dirt, dust, grease and/or various petroleum products.
  • High volume and noise-level industrial and production environments.
  • Intense bright light and extreme low-level lighted working conditions.
  • Cutting, metal shavings and welding slag.

Work Hours:

  • Standard work schedule.
  • Overtime required to meet deadlines, travel, and emergent conditions.
  • Off-shift work hours may be required.

Travel Requirements:

  • Remote Position that requires job responsibilities to be performed from customers work sites. This is not a work from home position.
  • This position is full travel position, with a 100% percent travel requirement.
  • Travel requires a minimum of two-week intervals between work site and employee domicile.
  • International travel may be required; employee could be expected to meet international requirements for entry.

Physical Demands:

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Please see Human Resources for detailed information for each physical demand.

  • Ascending or descending ladders, stairs, scaffolding, ramps, poles and the like, using feet and legs and/or hands and arms.
  • Medium work that includes moving objects up to 50 pounds.
  • Moving about on foot to accomplish tasks, particularly for long distances or moving from one work site to another.

The Center for Biological Diversity’s Southwest Program is hiring a Law Clerk for Summer 2027 to support conservation of imperiled species and public lands in Arizona, New Mexico, and on Utah’s Colorado Plateau. The Law Clerk will gain experience in legal research and writing, and environmental advocacy, drawing on litigation, science, media, and grassroots organizing strategies to fight for wildlife and their habitats in the Southwest.

This position is remote, but remote work from any of the Center office’s may be available based on office capacity. The expectation is that the Law Clerk will work full-time hours (40 hours per week) for ten weeks, but other arrangements may be considered.

To apply, please upload a:

  1. cover letter explaining your interest in clerking in the Center’s Southwest program;
  1. resume;
  2. writing sample, preferably of no more than 10 pages that reflects your own legal analysis;
  3. transcript (unofficial is fine); and
  1. list of three references.

Please submit all application materials via our website at.

Incomplete applications will not be considered. Application review will begin November 1, 2026, but applications will continue to be accepted until the position is filled. The desired start date is May 17, 2027. You will be notified if you are selected for an interview. No telephone calls, please.

ABOUT THE CENTER
The Center for Biological Diversity, a national 501(c)(3) non-profit organization, believes the welfare of human beings is deeply linked to nature — to the existence of a vast diversity of wild animals, plants, and people. Because diversity has intrinsic value, and because its loss impoverishes society, we work to secure a future for all species, great and small, hovering on the brink of extinction. We do so through science, law, activism, and creative media, with a focus on protecting the lands, waters, and climate that humans, other species, and all communities need to survive and thrive.

We want those who come after us to inherit a world where the wild is still alive.

POSITION SUMMARY

The Law Clerk will work in the Southwest program to protect imperiled species and public lands in Arizona, New Mexico, and on the Colorado Plateau. The Southwest program defends imperiled species and their habitats from agency actions and seizes proactive opportunities to protect and re-establish those species and habitats. Primary duties of this position include supporting impact litigation and administrative and policy advocacy to address key threats to imperiled species and advance program campaigns. Familiarity with Southwest regional issues and dynamics is desired but not required. The Law Clerk will work with experienced attorneys who provide supervision, training, and mentorship. The working environment is dynamic, exciting and supportive.

ESSENTIAL JOB DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Conduct legal research and writing, including preparing legal memoranda, assisting with brief writing, preparing filings, investigating new projects, and drafting public comments;
  • Review administrative regulations and other policy proposals;
  • May have opportunities to observe court arguments or agency proceedings;
  • Collaborate with diverse coalitions and partners;
  • Analyze federal and state legislation relating to endangered species, public lands, and environmental protection;
  • Perform other job-related duties as assigned; and
  • Put boots on the ground in the wild places we protect.

AREAS IN WHICH SKILLS WILL BE GAINED

Clerks will gain experience in legal research and writing, and environmental advocacy, drawing on litigation, science, media, and grassroots organizing strategies to fight for wildlife and their habitats in the Southwest.

ESSENTIAL QUALIFICATIONS AND SKILLS

  • Completed at least one year of law school at time of application;
  • Strong legal research and writing skills;
  • Passionate about protecting wildlife and their habitats in the Southwest;
  • Commitment to equity and justice;
  • Background or experience in natural resources, environmental, and/or administrative law preferred and scientific literacy preferred;
  • Strong work ethic, time management, and organizational skills;
  • Creativity and motivation.

WORKING CONDITIONS

Requires work in an in-person or at-home office setting, with a typical schedule of Monday-Friday with some night and weekend work required at times due to deadlines. May need to use typical office equipment such as computers, printers, copiers, etc.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS
